grammarPages.explanation: This pattern is used to indicate something which begins with a point in time. “起” serves as a verb here and means “to begin”. “從” is often followed by time words or verb phrases, e.g., “從下個月起” and “從開始學中文起”. Besides, “就” is often used at the beginning of the latter clause to imply an action is going to occur. In this pattern, “從” can be omitted. The subject can be placed in the beginning of the sentence or the second clause.
grammarPages.explanationEnglish: This pattern is used to indicate something which begins with a point in time. “起” serves as a verb here and means “to begin”. “從” is often followed by time words or verb phrases, e.g., “從下個月起” and “從開始學中文起”. Besides, “就” is often used at the beginning of the latter clause to imply an action is going to occur. In this pattern, “從” can be omitted. The subject can be placed in the beginning of the sentence or the second clause.
grammarPages.sourceExplanationEnglish: This pattern is used to indicate something which begins with a point in time. “起” serves as a verb here and means “to begin”. “從” is often followed by time words or verb phrases, e.g., “從下個月起” and “從開始學中文起”. Besides, “就” is often used at the beginning of the latter clause to imply an action is going to occur. In this pattern, “從” can be omitted. The subject can be placed in the beginning of the sentence or the second clause.

text.traditional: 從明天起，他就要天天早起去慢跑。
text.simplified: 从明天起，他就要天天早起去慢跑。
text.pinyin: Cóng míngtiān qǐ, tā jiùyào tiāntiān zǎo qǐ qù mànpǎo.
text.english: Starting tomorrow, he will get up early to jog every day.

text.traditional: 姐姐從學會開車起，就自己開車去上班了。
text.simplified: 姐姐从学会开车起，就自己开车去上班了。
text.pinyin: Jiějie cóng xuéhuì kāichē qǐ, jiù zìjǐ kāichē qù shàngbān le.
text.english: As soon as my older sister learned to drive, she started driving herself to work.

text.traditional: 為了身體健康，（從）明天起，我就不吃太甜、太油的食物了。
text.simplified: 为了身体健康，（从）明天起，我就不吃太甜、太油的食物了。
text.pinyin: Wèile shēntǐ jiànkāng, (cóng) míngtiān qǐ, wǒ jiù bù chī tài tián, tài yóu de shíwù le.
text.english: For my health, starting tomorrow I will stop eating food that is too sweet or greasy.

summary: This pattern says something starts from a certain time or action. 起 means begin.
從 often goes before a time word or verb phrase, and it can be left out.
就 often starts the second part. The subject can go at the start or in the second part.

grammarPages.lessonTitleEnglish: A Small Clerk? A Big Boss?
grammarPages.learnerPromise: Use 向 before a person to mark the recipient of an action; it is more formal and respectful than 跟.
grammarPages.pattern: 向 + N／NP + V……
grammarPages.explanation: “向” can be used as a preposition that shows the direction of an action, e.g., “向前走”. If followed by a person, it indicates the object of an action. This pattern is more formal, polite and respectful than the pattern “跟+N/NP+V”.
grammarPages.explanationEnglish: “向” can be used as a preposition that shows the direction of an action, e.g., “向前走”. If followed by a person, it indicates the object of an action. This pattern is more formal, polite and respectful than the pattern “跟+N/NP+V”.
grammarPages.sourceExplanationEnglish: “向” can be used as a preposition that shows the direction of an action, e.g., “向前走”. If followed by a person, it indicates the object of an action. This pattern is more formal, polite and respectful than the pattern “跟+N/NP+V”.

text.traditional: 餐廳的老闆向客人介紹那個義大利菜。
text.simplified: 餐厅的老板向客人介绍那个义大利菜。
text.pinyin: Cāntīng de lǎobǎn xiàng kèrén jièshào nàge Yìdàlì cài.
text.english: The restaurant owner introduces that Italian dish to the customers.

text.traditional: 這個研究計畫有問題，我應該向教授報告。
text.simplified: 这个研究计划有问题，我应该向教授报告。
text.pinyin: Zhège yánjiù jìhuà yǒu wèntí, wǒ yīnggāi xiàng jiàoshòu bàogào.
text.english: There is a problem with this research project; I should report it to the professor.

text.traditional: 那個學生很認真，成績也很好，我們都應該向他學習。
text.simplified: 那个学生很认真，成绩也很好，我们都应该向他学习。
text.pinyin: Nàge xuéshēng hěn rènzhēn, chéngjī yě hěn hǎo, wǒmen dōu yīnggāi xiàng tā xuéxí.
text.english: That student is diligent and gets good grades; we should all learn from him.

summary: 向 can show the direction of an action. Before a person, it shows who the action is aimed at.
Compared with 跟, 向 sounds more formal, polite and respectful.

grammarPages.lessonTitleEnglish: A Small Clerk? A Big Boss?
grammarPages.learnerPromise: Link a known fact to the conclusion it makes unsurprising.
grammarPages.pattern: Reason or known fact + 難怪 + result
grammarPages.explanation: Before “難怪”, there is usually an existing fact stated and unlikely to change, so no need to feel surprised. “難怪” is often followed by verb phrases. Sometimes when used in a conversation, the listener will be a little surprised after understanding a stated fact or reason.
grammarPages.explanationEnglish: Before “難怪”, there is usually an existing fact stated and unlikely to change, so no need to feel surprised. “難怪” is often followed by verb phrases. Sometimes when used in a conversation, the listener will be a little surprised after understanding a stated fact or reason.
grammarPages.sourceExplanationEnglish: Before “難怪”, there is usually an existing fact stated and unlikely to change, so no need to feel surprised. “難怪” is often followed by verb phrases. Sometimes when used in a conversation, the listener will be a little surprised after understanding a stated fact or reason.

text.traditional: 他喝了太多酒，難怪身體不舒服。
text.simplified: 他喝了太多酒，难怪身体不舒服。
text.pinyin: Tā hē le tài duō jiǔ, nánguài shēntǐ bù shūfu.
text.english: He drank too much alcohol; no wonder he feels unwell.

text.traditional: 那個美國人在中國住了五年，難怪中文說得那麼好。
text.simplified: 那个美国人在中国住了五年，难怪中文说得那么好。
text.pinyin: Nàge Měiguó rén zài Zhōngguó zhù le wǔ nián, nánguài Zhōngwén shuō de nàme hǎo.
text.english: That American lived in China for five years; no wonder they speak Chinese so well.

text.traditional: 同事 A：經理說他感冒了，昨天晚上不但發燒，還一直咳嗽。同事 B：難怪他今天上班的時候，一直戴著口罩。
text.simplified: 同事 A：经理说他感冒了，昨天晚上不但发烧，还一直咳嗽。同事 B：难怪他今天上班的时候，一直戴着口罩。
text.pinyin: Tóngshì A: Jīnglǐ shuō tā gǎnmào le, zuótiān wǎnshàng búdàn fāshāo, hái yìzhí késòu. Tóngshì B: Nánguài tā jīntiān shàngbān de shíhòu, yìzhí dài zhe kǒuzhào.
text.english: Coworker A: The manager said he has a cold. Last night he not only had a fever, but also kept coughing. Coworker B: No wonder he kept wearing a mask at work today.

summary: 難怪 says a result is no surprise, now that you know the reason.
The known fact usually comes first, then 難怪 and the result.
A verb phrase often follows 難怪, and it can also start a reply in conversation.

grammarPages.lessonTitleEnglish: A Small Clerk? A Big Boss?
grammarPages.titleEnglish: Can or Can’t Manage: V得了／V不了
grammarPages.learnerPromise: Say whether someone can accomplish an action or achieve a result.
grammarPages.pattern: V + 得了／不了（+ O）
grammarPages.explanation: The pattern “V 得了” shows one’s ability to achieve something or cause a certain result. Its negative form is “V 不了”. The verbs used in this pattern are often monosyllabic, such as “吃（eat）”, “忘（forget）”, “拿（take）”, “做（do）”, “到（reach）”, “管（manage）”, etc. This pattern is different from “V 了”. The former shows likelihood, while the latter implies that something has been done, e.g., “吃了” and “做了”.
grammarPages.explanationEnglish: The pattern “V 得了” shows one’s ability to achieve something or cause a certain result. Its negative form is “V 不了”. The verbs used in this pattern are often monosyllabic, such as “吃（eat）”, “忘（forget）”, “拿（take）”, “做（do）”, “到（reach）”, “管（manage）”, etc. This pattern is different from “V 了”. The former shows likelihood, while the latter implies that something has been done, e.g., “吃了” and “做了”.
grammarPages.sourceExplanationEnglish: The pattern “V 得了” shows one’s ability to achieve something or cause a certain result. Its negative form is “V 不了”. The verbs used in this pattern are often monosyllabic, such as “吃（eat）”, “忘（forget）”, “拿（take）”, “做（do）”, “到（reach）”, “管（manage）”, etc. This pattern is different from “V 了”. The former shows likelihood, while the latter implies that something has been done, e.g., “吃了” and “做了”.

text.traditional: 你買了這麼多東西，一個人拿得了嗎？
text.simplified: 你买了这么多东西，一个人拿得了吗？
text.pinyin: Nǐ mǎi le zhème duō dōngxi, yígerén ná de liǎo ma?
text.english: You bought so many things. Can one person carry them all?

text.traditional: 我們只有三個人，吃不了這麼多菜。
text.simplified: 我们只有三个人，吃不了这么多菜。
text.pinyin: Wǒmen zhǐyǒu sān ge rén, chī bùliǎo zhème duō cài.
text.english: There are only three of us; we can’t eat this many dishes.

text.traditional: 媽媽一個人做不了那麼多家事，所以我的房間自己打掃。
text.simplified: 妈妈一个人做不了那么多家事，所以我的房间自己打扫。
text.pinyin: Māma yígerén zuò bùliǎo nàme duō jiāshì, suǒyǐ wǒ de fángjiān zìjǐ dǎsǎo.
text.english: Mom can’t do so many chores alone, so I clean my own room.

summary: V得了 says you can do the action or reach the result. The negative is V不了.
It often goes with a verb of one syllable.
It is about being able to do it. V了 is different, because it says the action is done.

items.title: Grammar 7–8 · A Small Clerk? A Big Boss?

dialogue.title: 短文 · 自我推薦 · A Letter of Self-Recommendation

text.traditional: 李老闆：
text.simplified: 李老板：
text.pinyin: Lǐ lǎobǎn:
text.english: Dear Mr. Li,

text.traditional: 您好，我是陳可欣，今年二十一歲，是大學日文系的學生。父親在高中教書，母親是鐵路局的員工，哥哥在貿易公司上班。我是家裡最小的孩子，可是我知道怎麼照顧自己，不讓父母擔心。
text.simplified: 您好，我是陈可欣，今年二十一岁，是大学日文系的学生。父亲在高中教书，母亲是铁路局的员工，哥哥在贸易公司上班。我是家里最小的孩子，可是我知道怎么照顾自己，不让父母担心。
text.pinyin: Nín hǎo, wǒ shì Chén Kěxīn, jīnnián èrshíyī suì, shì dàxué Rìwén xì de xuéshēng. Fùqīn zài gāozhōng jiāoshū, mǔqīn shì Tiělùjú de yuángōng, gēge zài màoyì gōngsī shàngbān. Wǒ shì jiālǐ zuì xiǎo de háizi, kěshì wǒ zhīdào zěnme zhàogù zìjǐ, bú ràng fùmǔ dānxīn.
text.english: I am Kexin Chen, 21 years old. I am a university student in the Department of Japanese Language. My father teaches in a senior high school, my mother is an employee in the Railways Administration, and my elder brother works in a trading company. I am the youngest in my family, but I know how to take care of myself, so I don’t let my parents worry about me.

text.traditional: 這個暑假，您要找人到鄉下的花園去種花、剪草。我不喜歡都市緊張的生活，也不習慣天天穿著襯衫，坐在辦公室裡打電腦。鄉下環境好、空氣新鮮，如果能在花園打工，不但可以認識很多植物，休息的時候，還可以坐在草地上喝個茶、聽個音樂。這樣的生活，一定會讓我很開心的。
text.simplified: 这个暑假，您要找人到乡下的花园去种花、剪草。我不喜欢都市紧张的生活，也不习惯天天穿着衬衫，坐在办公室里打电脑。乡下环境好、空气新鲜，如果能在花园打工，不但可以认识很多植物，休息的时候，还可以坐在草地上喝个茶、听个音乐。这样的生活，一定会让我很开心的。
text.pinyin: Zhège shǔjià, nín yào zhǎo rén dào xiāngxià de huāyuán qù zhòng huā, jiǎn cǎo. Wǒ bù xǐhuān dūshì jǐnzhāng de shēnghuó, yě bù xíguàn tiāntiān chuān zhe chènshān, zuò zài bàngōngshì lǐ dǎ diànnǎo. Xiāngxià huánjìng hǎo, kōngqì xīnxiān, rúguǒ néng zài huāyuán dǎgōng, búdàn kěyǐ rènshì hěn duō zhíwù, xiūxí de shíhòu, hái kěyǐ zuò zài cǎodì shàng hē ge chá, tīng ge yīnyuè. Zhèyàng de shēnghuó, yídìng huì ràng wǒ hěn kāixīn de.
text.english: This summer vacation, you are looking for people who will grow flowers and trim the lawn in a countryside garden. I don’t like stressful urban life, and I am not used to wearing a shirt every day or sitting in an office using a computer. In the countryside the environment is good, and the air is fresh. If I can work part-time in a garden, I can not only know many plants, but also sit on the grass drinking tea or listen to some music during the breaks. This kind of life will certainly make me happy!

text.traditional: 我現在沒有正式的職業，可是我知道打工的經驗很重要，能讓我有不少的收穫。比如說，可以存一點兒學費，學習做事的方法，讓自己的想法更成熟、工作能力更強。大二時，我為了加強日文的會話能力，就去當教授的助理；也做過日本餐廳的服務生、去工廠打過工。洗碗、打掃或是搬重的東西，我都自己來。有時候工作到夜裡兩、三點才回家，我也不害怕。
text.simplified: 我现在没有正式的职业，可是我知道打工的经验很重要，能让我有不少的收获。比如说，可以存一点儿学费，学习做事的方法，让自己的想法更成熟、工作能力更强。大二时，我为了加强日文的会话能力，就去当教授的助理；也做过日本餐厅的服务生、去工厂打过工。洗碗、打扫或是搬重的东西，我都自己来。有时候工作到夜里两、三点才回家，我也不害怕。
text.pinyin: Wǒ xiànzài méiyǒu zhèngshì de zhíyè, kěshì wǒ zhīdào dǎgōng de jīngyàn hěn zhòngyào, néng ràng wǒ yǒu bùshǎo de shōuhuò. Bǐrú shuō, kěyǐ cún yìdiǎnr xuéfèi, xuéxí zuòshì de fāngfǎ, ràng zìjǐ de xiǎngfǎ gèng chéngshú, gōngzuò nénglì gèng qiáng. Dà èr shí, wǒ wèile jiāqiáng Rìwén de huìhuà nénglì, jiù qù dāng jiàoshòu de zhùlǐ; yě zuò guo Rìběn cāntīng de fúwùshēng, qù gōngchǎng dǎ guo gōng. Xǐwǎn, dǎsǎo huòshì bān zhòng de dōngxi, wǒ dōu zìjǐ lái. Yǒushíhòu gōngzuò dào yèlǐ liǎng, sān diǎn cái huí jiā, wǒ yě bú hàipà.
text.english: I don’t have a formal job now, but I know that part-time working experience is very important, and it benefits me a lot. For example, I can save some money for the tuition, learn how to do some tasks, and become more mature in thinking and have stronger working ability. In my sophomore year, in order to improve my Japanese conversation ability, I worked as a professor’s assistant. I also worked as a waitress in a Japanese restaurant. I did all tasks such as doing dishes, cleaning, or moving heavy objects by myself. Sometimes I worked until 2 or 3 a.m. before going back home, but I wasn’t afraid, either.

text.traditional: 我是一個很樂觀的人，也相信有能力把您的花園照顧好，所以向您推薦我自己，請給我這個工作機會。從現在起，我的手機二十四小時都開著，有好消息的話，請隨時通知我，非常謝謝您！
text.simplified: 我是一个很乐观的人，也相信有能力把您的花园照顾好，所以向您推荐我自己，请给我这个工作机会。从现在起，我的手机二十四小时都开着，有好消息的话，请随时通知我，非常谢谢您！
text.pinyin: Wǒ shì yíge hěn lèguān de rén, yě xiāngxìn yǒu nénglì bǎ nín de huāyuán zhàogù hǎo, suǒyǐ xiàng nín tuījiàn wǒ zìjǐ, qǐng gěi wǒ zhège gōngzuò jīhuì. Cóng xiànzài qǐ, wǒ de shǒujī èrshísì xiǎoshí dōu kāi zhe, yǒu hǎo xiāoxí dehuà, qǐng suíshí tōngzhī wǒ, fēicháng xièxie nín!
text.english: I am a very optimistic person. I believe I have the ability to take good care of your garden. Therefore, I recommend myself to you. Please give me this job opportunity. From now on, you can reach me on my phone 24 hours a day. If you have any good news, please inform me any time. Thank you very much!

text.traditional: 陳可欣　敬上
text.simplified: 陈可欣敬上
text.pinyin: Chén Kěxīn jìngshàng
text.english: Sincerely, Kexin Chen

text.traditional: 5 月 21 日
text.simplified: 5 月 21 日
text.pinyin: 5 yuè 21 rì
text.english: May 21st

grammarPages.lessonTitleEnglish: A Small Clerk? A Big Boss?
grammarPages.learnerPromise: Use 個 after a verb to make an action sound brief, casual, or easy.
grammarPages.pattern: V + 個 + N（O）
grammarPages.explanation: In this pattern, “個” serves as a particle showing that an action only lasts for a short time or something is done in a relaxing and easy manner. Verb-object separable words are often used in this pattern, such as “喝個茶”, “唱個歌”, “跳個舞”, etc.
grammarPages.explanationEnglish: In this pattern, “個” serves as a particle showing that an action only lasts for a short time or something is done in a relaxing and easy manner. Verb-object separable words are often used in this pattern, such as “喝個茶”, “唱個歌”, “跳個舞”, etc.
grammarPages.sourceExplanationEnglish: In this pattern, “個” serves as a particle showing that an action only lasts for a short time or something is done in a relaxing and easy manner. Verb-object separable words are often used in this pattern, such as “喝個茶”, “唱個歌”, “跳個舞”, etc.

text.traditional: 我覺得洗個碗、倒個垃圾都是很簡單的家事。
text.simplified: 我觉得洗个碗、倒个垃圾都是很简单的家事。
text.pinyin: Wǒ juéde xǐ ge wǎn, dào ge lèsè dōu shì hěn jiǎndān de jiāshì.
text.english: I think washing a few dishes and taking out the trash are both very simple chores.

text.traditional: 爸爸每天下班回家，都先看個電視再吃晚飯。
text.simplified: 爸爸每天下班回家，都先看个电视再吃晚饭。
text.pinyin: Bàba měitiān xiàbān huí jiā, dōu xiān kàn ge diànshì zài chī wǎnfàn.
text.english: When Dad comes home from work each day, he watches a little TV before dinner.

text.traditional: 這個週末我想先去 KTV 唱個歌，再去看個電影，輕鬆一下。
text.simplified: 这个周末我想先去 KTV 唱个歌，再去看个电影，轻松一下。
text.pinyin: Zhè ge zhōumò wǒ xiǎng xiān qù KTV chàng ge gē, zài qù kàn ge diànyǐng, qīngsōng yíxià.
text.english: This weekend I want to go to KTV first for a bit of singing, then catch a movie and relax a little.

summary: 個 after a verb makes the action sound short, relaxed or easy.
Words made of a verb and its object often use this form, such as 喝個茶.

grammarPages.lessonTitleEnglish: A Small Clerk? A Big Boss?
grammarPages.titleEnglish: Letting Someone Do It: N 來 V
grammarPages.learnerPromise: Use 來 to stand for a known action, or let someone else handle a task.
grammarPages.pattern: N／NP + 來（+ V）
grammarPages.explanation: In this pattern, “來” refers to an omitted verb and is often used when there is a specific action, e.g., “我來做” and “我來幫忙”. If the dialogue responds with “自己來”, it indicates that the speaker doesn’t want to bother the other person. It is a polite statement.
grammarPages.explanationEnglish: In this pattern, “來” refers to an omitted verb and is often used when there is a specific action, e.g., “我來做” and “我來幫忙”. If the dialogue responds with “自己來”, it indicates that the speaker doesn’t want to bother the other person. It is a polite statement.
grammarPages.sourceExplanationEnglish: In this pattern, “來” refers to an omitted verb and is often used when there is a specific action, e.g., “我來做” and “我來幫忙”. If the dialogue responds with “自己來”, it indicates that the speaker doesn’t want to bother the other person. It is a polite statement.

text.traditional: 我做了很多菜，你想吃什麼，自己來，別客氣。
text.simplified: 我做了很多菜，你想吃什么，自己来，别客气。
text.pinyin: Wǒ zuò le hěn duō cài, nǐ xiǎng chī shénme, zìjǐ lái, bié kèqì.
text.english: I made a lot of dishes. Help yourself to whatever you want; don’t be shy.

text.traditional: 上網訂票、找資料、寫報告，這些事情李老闆都讓助理來。
text.simplified: 上网订票、找资料、写报告，这些事情李老板都让助理来。
text.pinyin: Shàngwǎng dìng piào, zhǎo zīliào, xiě bàogào, zhèxiē shìqíng Lǐ lǎobǎn dōu ràng zhùlǐ lái.
text.english: For booking tickets online, finding information, and writing reports, Mr. Li has his assistant handle all those things.

text.traditional: A：像洗碗、打掃房間這樣的事，那個孩子都做不好。B：他才五歲，這些事最好讓父母來（做）。
text.simplified: A：像洗碗、打扫房间这样的事，那个孩子都做不好。B：他才五岁，这些事最好让父母来（做）。
text.pinyin: A: Xiàng xǐwǎn, dǎsǎo fángjiān zhèyàng de shì, nàge háizi dōu zuò bùhǎo. B: Tā cái wǔ suì, zhèxiē shì zuìhǎo ràng fùmǔ lái (zuò).
text.english: A: The child cannot do things like washing dishes and cleaning the room well. B: He is only five; it’s best to let his parents do those things.

summary: 來 stands in for an action that is already clear from the context, often a specific one.
自己來 is a polite way to say you don't want to trouble someone else.

items.title: Grammar 1–3 · I Want to Buy a Laptop

grammarPages.lessonTitleEnglish: I Want to Buy a Laptop
grammarPages.titleEnglish: No Matter What with 不管…都…
grammarPages.learnerPromise: State a result that stays true under every condition.
grammarPages.pattern: 不管 + question/condition，(subject) + 都 + unchanged result
grammarPages.explanation: This pattern indicates in every possible condition, the stated situation in the latter part of the sentence will not change. “不管” is followed by possible conditions, and “都” is followed by the situation that will remain unchanged. Besides, the sentence following “不管” is an interrogative sentence, which can be Wh-Question, A-not-A Question, Alternative Question, and two opposite monosyllabic words.
grammarPages.explanationEnglish: This pattern indicates in every possible condition, the stated situation in the latter part of the sentence will not change. “不管” is followed by possible conditions, and “都” is followed by the situation that will remain unchanged. Besides, the sentence following “不管” is an interrogative sentence, which can be Wh-Question, A-not-A Question, Alternative Question, and two opposite monosyllabic words.
grammarPages.sourceExplanationEnglish: This pattern indicates in every possible condition, the stated situation in the latter part of the sentence will not change. “不管” is followed by possible conditions, and “都” is followed by the situation that will remain unchanged. Besides, the sentence following “不管” is an interrogative sentence, which can be Wh-Question, A-not-A Question, Alternative Question, and two opposite monosyllabic words.

text.traditional: 不管這支手機貴不貴，我都要買。
text.simplified: 不管这支手机贵不贵，我都要买。
text.pinyin: Bùguǎn zhè zhī shǒujī guì bú guì, wǒ dōu yào mǎi.
text.english: No matter whether this phone is expensive, I still want to buy it.

text.traditional: 不管看什麼電影，我都喜歡跟朋友一起看。
text.simplified: 不管看什么电影，我都喜欢跟朋友一起看。
text.pinyin: Bùguǎn kàn shénme diànyǐng, wǒ dōu xǐhuān gēn péngyǒu yìqǐ kàn.
text.english: No matter what movie it is, I like watching it with friends.

text.traditional: 這個城市交通便利，不管搭公車還是火車都很方便。
text.simplified: 这个城市交通便利，不管搭公车还是火车都很方便。
text.pinyin: Zhè ge chéngshì jiāotōng biànlì, bùguǎn dā gōngchē háishì huǒchē dōu hěn fāngbiàn.
text.english: Transportation in this city is convenient; it is easy to get around by either bus or train.

text.traditional: 員工：我今天心情不好，我要請假。老闆：不管心情好壞，你都得來上班。
text.simplified: 员工：我今天心情不好，我要请假。老板：不管心情好坏，你都得来上班。
text.pinyin: Yuángōng: Wǒ jīntiān xīnqíng bùhǎo, wǒ yào qǐngjià. Lǎobǎn: Bùguǎn xīnqíng hǎohuài, nǐ dōu děi lái shàngbān.
text.english: Employee: I’m in a bad mood today, so I want to take a day off. Boss: Whether you’re in a good or bad mood, you still have to come to work.

summary: 不管 ... 都 says that in every possible condition, the result stays the same.
After 不管 come the possible conditions, and after 都 comes the situation that does not change.
What follows 不管 is a question: a question word, A-not-A, a choice, or two opposite one-syllable words.

grammarPages.lessonTitleEnglish: I Want to Buy a Laptop
grammarPages.learnerPromise: Offer a better alternative after explaining the first option.
grammarPages.pattern: original action/comment，不如 + better suggestion (+ explanation)
grammarPages.explanation: This pattern in a conversation is usually used to help the speaker offer a better suggestion. Before “不如”, the speaker can give comments on the original action to explain why there is a better suggestion which follows “不如”. And, accordingly, a further explanation can be added to the better suggestion.
grammarPages.explanationEnglish: This pattern in a conversation is usually used to help the speaker offer a better suggestion. Before “不如”, the speaker can give comments on the original action to explain why there is a better suggestion which follows “不如”. And, accordingly, a further explanation can be added to the better suggestion.
grammarPages.sourceExplanationEnglish: This pattern in a conversation is usually used to help the speaker offer a better suggestion. Before “不如”, the speaker can give comments on the original action to explain why there is a better suggestion which follows “不如”. And, accordingly, a further explanation can be added to the better suggestion.

text.traditional: 這台筆電太舊了，如果要花不少錢修理，不如買一台新的。
text.simplified: 这台笔电太旧了，如果要花不少钱修理，不如买一台新的。
text.pinyin: Zhè tái bǐdiàn tài jiù le, rúguǒ yào huā bùshǎo qián xiūlǐ, bùrú mǎi yì tái xīn de.
text.english: This laptop is too old. If repairing it would cost a lot, it would be better to buy a new one.

text.traditional: 先生：那台最新的平板不但很輕，功能也很好，我想要買。太太：可是新產品都很貴，不如等便宜一點兒再買吧！
text.simplified: 先生：那台最新的平板不但很轻，功能也很好，我想要买。太太：可是新产品都很贵，不如等便宜一点儿再买吧！
text.pinyin: Xiānshēng: Nà tái zuìxīn de píngbǎn búdàn hěn qīng, gōngnéng yě hěn hǎo, wǒ xiǎngyào mǎi. Tàitai: Kěshì xīn chǎnpǐn dōu hěn guì, bùrú děng piányí yìdiǎnr zài mǎi ba!
text.english: Husband: That newest tablet is light and has great features. I want to buy it. Wife: But new products are all expensive. It would be better to wait until it’s a little cheaper.

text.traditional: A：我們去附近的飯館吃餃子，好不好？B：那家飯館常常客滿，不如去便利商店買三明治，不必等。
text.simplified: A：我们去附近的饭馆吃饺子，好不好？B：那家饭馆常常客满，不如去便利商店买三明治，不必等。
text.pinyin: A: Wǒmen qù fùjìn de fànguǎn chī jiǎozi, hǎo bù hǎo? B: Nà jiā fànguǎn chángcháng kèmǎn, bùrú qù biànlì shāngdiàn mǎi sānmíngzhì, búbì děng.
text.english: A: Shall we go to the nearby restaurant for dumplings? B: That restaurant is often full. We’d better go to the convenience store for a sandwich; we won’t have to wait.

summary: 不如 offers a better suggestion than the original action.
Before 不如, the speaker can comment on the original action to explain why.
After the suggestion, you can add a further explanation.

grammarPages.lessonTitleEnglish: I Want to Buy a Laptop
grammarPages.titleEnglish: A Little Too… with Vs了一點兒
grammarPages.learnerPromise: Describe a small shortcoming or complaint.
grammarPages.pattern: Vs + 了 +（一）點兒
grammarPages.explanation: This pattern is used when the speaker wants to show a situation is not as good as expected, but there is not much difference. Usually, it implies minor weaknesses or complaints. For example, “這支手機不錯，可是貴了一點兒 (This cell phone is not bad, but it is a little bit expensive.)” In the example, the speaker thinks the cell phone is more expensive than he expects, but it is not a big issue.
grammarPages.explanationEnglish: This pattern is used when the speaker wants to show a situation is not as good as expected, but there is not much difference. Usually, it implies minor weaknesses or complaints. For example, “這支手機不錯，可是貴了一點兒 (This cell phone is not bad, but it is a little bit expensive.)” In the example, the speaker thinks the cell phone is more expensive than he expects, but it is not a big issue.
grammarPages.sourceExplanationEnglish: This pattern is used when the speaker wants to show a situation is not as good as expected, but there is not much difference. Usually, it implies minor weaknesses or complaints. For example, “這支手機不錯，可是貴了一點兒 (This cell phone is not bad, but it is a little bit expensive.)” In the example, the speaker thinks the cell phone is more expensive than he expects, but it is not a big issue.

text.traditional: 這堂美術課很有意思，可是學生多了一點兒。
text.simplified: 这堂美术课很有意思，可是学生多了一点儿。
text.pinyin: Zhè táng měishù kè hěn yǒuyìsi, kěshì xuéshēng duō le yìdiǎnr.
text.english: This art class is interesting, but there are a bit too many students.

text.traditional: 健身雖然對身體有很多好處，但是健身房的費用高了一點兒。
text.simplified: 健身虽然对身体有很多好处，但是健身房的费用高了一点儿。
text.pinyin: Jiànshēn suīrán duì shēntǐ yǒu hěn duō hǎochù, dànshì jiànshēnfáng de fèiyòng gāo le yìdiǎnr.
text.english: Although working out has many benefits for your health, the gym fee is a little high.

text.traditional: A：聽說你趁這次春假去了日月潭，那裡的風景怎麼樣？B：日月潭很美，花也都開了。可惜人太多，擠了點兒。
text.simplified: A：听说你趁这次春假去了日月潭，那里的风景怎么样？B：日月潭很美，花也都开了。可惜人太多，挤了点儿。
text.pinyin: A: Tīngshuō nǐ chèn zhè cì chūnjià qù le Rìyuè Tán, nàlǐ de fēngjǐng zěnmeyàng? B: Rìyuè Tán hěn měi, huā yě dōu kāi le. Kěxí rén tài duō, jǐ le diǎnr.
text.english: A: I heard you went to Sun Moon Lake during spring break. How was the scenery? B: Sun Moon Lake is beautiful, and the flowers have all bloomed. Too bad there were so many people; it was a little crowded.

summary: 了一點兒 after a state word says something is not as good as expected, but not by much.
It usually shows small weaknesses or a mild complaint, like 貴了一點兒.

dialogue.title: 對話 · 我要買筆電 · I Want to Buy a Laptop

text.traditional: 您好，要找哪種產品？筆電還是平板？
text.simplified: 您好，要找哪种产品？笔电还是平板？
text.pinyin: Nín hǎo, yào zhǎo nǎ zhǒng chǎnpǐn? Bǐdiàn háishì píngbǎn?
text.english: Hello! What kind of product are you looking for? A laptop or a tablet?

text.traditional: 你好，請問這兩種有什麼差別？你可以說明一下嗎？
text.simplified: 你好，请问这两种有什么差别？你可以说明一下吗？
text.pinyin: Nǐ hǎo, qǐngwèn zhè liǎng zhǒng yǒu shénme chābié? Nǐ kěyǐ shuōmíng yíxià ma?
text.english: Hello. May I ask that what is the difference between these two? Could you please explain?

text.traditional: 其實功能都差不多，可是平板比較輕，不少上班族出差時，得隨時處理公司的事情，所以他們比較喜歡買平板。
text.simplified: 其实功能都差不多，可是平板比较轻，不少上班族出差时，得随时处理公司的事情，所以他们比较喜欢买平板。
text.pinyin: Qíshí gōngnéng dōu chàbùduō, kěshì píngbǎn bǐjiào qīng, bùshǎo shàngbān zú chūchāi shí, děi suíshí chǔlǐ gōngsī de shìqíng, suǒyǐ tāmen bǐjiào xǐhuān mǎi píngbǎn.
text.english: Actually, their functions are similar, but tablets are lighter. When many office workers go on business trips, they have to deal with tasks of their companies anytime, so they prefer buying tablets.

text.traditional: 你的意思是，帶著筆電出門很麻煩，不如買平板？
text.simplified: 你的意思是，带着笔电出门很麻烦，不如买平板？
text.pinyin: Nǐ de yìsi shì, dài zhe bǐdiàn chūmén hěn máfán, bùrú mǎi píngbǎn?
text.english: You mean it is very troublesome to go out with a laptop, and it is better to buy a laptop, right?

text.traditional: 也不一定，大多數的大學生把筆電放在背包裡，不管去圖書館還是咖啡廳，隨時都能做功課、寫報告。
text.simplified: 也不一定，大多数的大学生把笔电放在背包里，不管去图书馆还是咖啡厅，随时都能做功课、写报告。
text.pinyin: Yě bù yídìng, dàduōshù de dàxuéshēng bǎ bǐdiàn fàng zài bēibāo lǐ, bùguǎn qù túshūguǎn háishì kāfēitīng, suíshí dōu néng zuò gōngkè, xiě bàogào.
text.english: Not necessarily. Most university students put laptops in their backpacks. No matter where they go, to a library or to a café, they can do homework and write reports anytime.

text.traditional: 我好像比較需要這樣的產品。那有沒有輕一點兒的筆電？
text.simplified: 我好像比较需要这样的产品。那有没有轻一点儿的笔电？
text.pinyin: Wǒ hǎoxiàng bǐjiào xūyào zhèyàng de chǎnpǐn. Nà yǒu méiyǒu qīng yìdiǎnr de bǐdiàn?
text.english: I seem to need this kind of product more. In that case, do you have any laptop that is lighter?

text.traditional: 有，請跟我來。您看，這部筆電是最新的，牌子很有名，也非常輕。
text.simplified: 有，请跟我来。您看，这部笔电是最新的，牌子很有名，也非常轻。
text.pinyin: Yǒu, qǐng gēn wǒ lái. Nín kàn, zhè bù bǐdiàn shì zuìxīn de, páizi hěn yǒumíng, yě fēicháng qīng.
text.english: We do. Please follow me. Look! This laptop is the newest. The brand is very famous and the laptop is very light, too.

text.traditional: 看起來很好用，拿起來也很輕，可是最近電視新聞說這個牌子的筆電不好，很多人都抱怨電池有問題。
text.simplified: 看起来很好用，拿起来也很轻，可是最近电视新闻说这个牌子的笔电不好，很多人都抱怨电池有问题。
text.pinyin: Kànqǐlái hěn hǎoyòng, ná qǐ lái yě hěn qīng, kěshì zuìjìn diànshì xīnwén shuō zhège páizi de bǐdiàn bùhǎo, hěn duō rén dōu bàoyuàn diànchí yǒu wèntí.
text.english: It looks useful, and is very light to carry. However, recently, in TV news people say laptops of this brand are not good. Many people complain about problems with the battery.

text.traditional: 電腦用久了，有問題是正常的。以後有問題的話，您就帶著保證書來，我們會幫您免費修理的。
text.simplified: 电脑用久了，有问题是正常的。以后有问题的话，您就带着保证书来，我们会帮您免费修理的。
text.pinyin: Diànnǎo yòng jiǔ le, yǒu wèntí shì zhèngcháng de. Yǐhòu yǒu wèntí dehuà, nín jiù dài zhe bǎozhèngshū lái, wǒmen huì bāng nín miǎnfèi xiūlǐ de.
text.english: If a computer has been used for a long time, it would be normal to have some problems. If there is really something wrong with it, you can bring this warranty, and we will repair it for you for free.

text.traditional: 這樣啊，不過三萬六千塊貴了一點兒，恐怕我買不起。我改天再來看看，謝謝。
text.simplified: 这样啊，不过三万六千块贵了一点儿，恐怕我买不起。我改天再来看看，谢谢。
text.pinyin: Zhèyàng a, búguò sānwànliùqiān kuài guì le yìdiǎnr, kǒngpà wǒ mǎi bù qǐ. Wǒ gǎitiān zài lái kànkan, xièxie.
text.english: I see. But a computer costing 36,000 dollars is a little expensive. I’m afraid I can’t afford it. I’ll come again another day, thank you.

text.traditional: 請等一下！除了傳真機，我們的產品這個禮拜都打八五折，還有「滿三萬送三千」的活動。
text.simplified: 请等一下！除了传真机，我们的产品这个礼拜都打八五折，还有「满三万送三千」的活动。
text.pinyin: Qǐng děng yíxià! Chúle chuánzhēnjī, wǒmen de chǎnpǐn zhège lǐbài dōu dǎ bāwǔ zhé, háiyǒu “mǎn sānwàn sòng sānqiān” de huódòng.
text.english: Please wait a moment! In addition to fax machines, our products are 15% off this week. We are also having a sales promotion, which is “3,000-dollar cash rebate on every 30,000-dollar purchase”.

text.traditional: 你的意思是打折以後要是超過三萬元，還可以再便宜三千塊嗎？
text.simplified: 你的意思是打折以后要是超过三万元，还可以再便宜三千块吗？
text.pinyin: Nǐ de yìsi shì dǎzhé yǐhòu yàoshì chāoguò sānwàn yuán, hái kěyǐ zài piányí sānqiān kuài ma?
text.english: Do you mean that if the price of the product after the discount exceeds 30,000 dollars, it can be another 3,000 dollars cheaper?

text.traditional: 沒錯，而且這個活動下禮拜就結束了，請把握機會喔！
text.simplified: 没错，而且这个活动下礼拜就结束了，请把握机会喔！
text.pinyin: Méicuò, érqiě zhège huódòng xià lǐbài jiù jiéshù le, qǐng bǎwò jīhuì o!
text.english: Exactly. What’s more, this offer will end next week. Please seize the opportunity!

text.traditional: 那麼，我只要付大約兩萬八，就能夠把這部筆電帶回家，是嗎？
text.simplified: 那么，我只要付大约两万八，就能够把这部笔电带回家，是吗？
text.pinyin: Nàme, wǒ zhǐyào fù dàyuē liǎngwànbā, jiù nénggòu bǎ zhè bù bǐdiàn dài huí jiā, shì ma?
text.english: So, I only need to pay about 28,000 dollars to bring the laptop home, right?

text.traditional: 是的。我們有白色、黑色、紅色等三種顏色讓客人選擇。
text.simplified: 是的。我们有白色、黑色、红色等三种颜色让客人选择。
text.pinyin: Shì de. Wǒmen yǒu báisè, hēisè, hóngsè děng sān zhǒng yánsè ràng kèrén xuǎnzé.
text.english: Yes, and we have three colors, white, black and red for our guests to choose.

text.traditional: 我要黑色的。
text.simplified: 我要黑色的。
text.pinyin: Wǒ yào hēisè de.
text.english: I’ll take the black one.

text.traditional: 好的。打折後是兩萬七千六百元，再送您一個真皮的背包。
text.simplified: 好的。打折后是两万七千六百元，再送您一个真皮的背包。
text.pinyin: Hǎo de. Dǎzhé hòu shì liǎngwànqīqiānliùbǎi yuán, zài sòng nín yíge zhēnpí de bēibāo.
text.english: Alright. That would be 27,600 dollars with the discount. I’ll give you a backpack made of genuine leather as a gift.

text.traditional: 謝謝，再見。
text.simplified: 谢谢，再见。
text.pinyin: Xièxie, zàijiàn.
text.english: Thank you. Goodbye.

text.traditional: 先生，這支手機是您的嗎？
text.simplified: 先生，这支手机是您的吗？
text.pinyin: Xiānshēng, zhè zhī shǒujī shì nín de ma?
text.english: Sir, is this cellphone yours?

items.title: Grammar 4–6 · I Want to Buy a Laptop

grammarPages.lessonTitleEnglish: I Want to Buy a Laptop
grammarPages.titleEnglish: Comparing with 比, 比較 and 比起來
grammarPages.learnerPromise: Compare two things with 比, 比較, or 比起來.
grammarPages.pattern: A 比 B + Vs / S + 比較 + Vs / 跟 B 比起來，A 比較……

columns.meaning: A is more/less Vs than B

columns.traditional: 跟 B 比起來，A 比較……
columns.simplified: 跟 B 比起来，A 比较……
columns.meaning: compared with B, A is more/less…

grammarPages.explanation: “比” is a preposition that indicates the status of the subject when a comparison is made. “比” is followed by the compared object, e.g., “我比你高” and “搭公車比搭火車便宜”, equivalent to “than” in English. “比較” is an adverb that indicates a higher or lower degree, e.g., “台灣比較熱” and “坐公車比較便宜”, equivalent to “more” in English. The subject is placed before “比較”, while the stative verb is placed after it. “比起來” is a phrase that shows the remark about one thing as compared to another. The common pattern is “(A/B)跟 B/A 比起來，A/B 比較……”, e.g., “（你）跟他比起來，你比較漂亮” and “（我）跟你比起來，我沒有你那麼漂亮”.
grammarPages.explanationEnglish: “比” is a preposition that indicates the status of the subject when a comparison is made. “比” is followed by the compared object, e.g., “我比你高” and “搭公車比搭火車便宜”, equivalent to “than” in English. “比較” is an adverb that indicates a higher or lower degree, e.g., “台灣比較熱” and “坐公車比較便宜”, equivalent to “more” in English. The subject is placed before “比較”, while the stative verb is placed after it. “比起來” is a phrase that shows the remark about one thing as compared to another. The common pattern is “(A/B)跟 B/A 比起來，A/B 比較……”, e.g., “（你）跟他比起來，你比較漂亮” and “（我）跟你比起來，我沒有你那麼漂亮”.
grammarPages.sourceExplanationEnglish: “比” is a preposition that indicates the status of the subject when a comparison is made. “比” is followed by the compared object, e.g., “我比你高” and “搭公車比搭火車便宜”, equivalent to “than” in English. “比較” is an adverb that indicates a higher or lower degree, e.g., “台灣比較熱” and “坐公車比較便宜”, equivalent to “more” in English. The subject is placed before “比較”, while the stative verb is placed after it. “比起來” is a phrase that shows the remark about one thing as compared to another. The common pattern is “(A/B)跟 B/A 比起來，A/B 比較……”, e.g., “（你）跟他比起來，你比較漂亮” and “（我）跟你比起來，我沒有你那麼漂亮”.

text.traditional: 平板比筆電便宜，所以我比較想買平板。
text.simplified: 平板比笔电便宜，所以我比较想买平板。
text.pinyin: Píngbǎn bǐ bǐdiàn piányí, suǒyǐ wǒ bǐjiào xiǎng mǎi píngbǎn.
text.english: Tablets are cheaper than laptops, so I’d rather buy a tablet.

text.traditional: 跟國外旅遊比起來，大部分的國內旅遊便宜一點兒。
text.simplified: 跟国外旅游比起来，大部分的国内旅游便宜一点儿。
text.pinyin: Gēn guówài lǚyóu bǐ qǐ lái, dàbùfèn de guónèi lǚyóu piányí yìdiǎnr.
text.english: Compared with traveling abroad, most domestic trips are a little cheaper.

text.traditional: 雖然筆電的功能比平板好，可是跟平板比起來，筆電比較重。
text.simplified: 虽然笔电的功能比平板好，可是跟平板比起来，笔电比较重。
text.pinyin: Suīrán bǐdiàn de gōngnéng bǐ píngbǎn hǎo, kěshì gēn píngbǎn bǐ qǐ lái, bǐdiàn bǐjiào zhòng.
text.english: Although laptops have better features than tablets, laptops are heavier compared with tablets.

summary: 比 means than. The thing you compare with goes after it: 我比你高.
比較 means more. The subject goes before it and the state verb goes after it.
比起來 gives a remark about one thing compared with another, often as 跟 B 比起來.

grammarPages.lessonTitleEnglish: I Want to Buy a Laptop
grammarPages.learnerPromise: Describe something unwanted that nearly happened.
grammarPages.pattern: 差（一）點兒 + verb phrase (+ 就 + result)
grammarPages.explanation: “差一點兒” is usually followed by verbs or verb phrases. This pattern is usually used in a situation when something which the speaker did not wish almost happened.
grammarPages.explanationEnglish: “差一點兒” is usually followed by verbs or verb phrases. This pattern is usually used in a situation when something which the speaker did not wish almost happened.
grammarPages.sourceExplanationEnglish: “差一點兒” is usually followed by verbs or verb phrases. This pattern is usually used in a situation when something which the speaker did not wish almost happened.

text.traditional: 我以為我的手機不見了，差一點兒就要去買新的。
text.simplified: 我以为我的手机不见了，差一点儿就要去买新的。
text.pinyin: Wǒ yǐwéi wǒ de shǒujī bújiànle, chàyìdiǎnr jiùyào qù mǎi xīn de.
text.english: I thought I had lost my phone and almost went to buy a new one.

text.traditional: 他吃了不新鮮的食物，拉了三天的肚子，差一點兒就死了。
text.simplified: 他吃了不新鲜的食物，拉了三天的肚子，差一点儿就死了。
text.pinyin: Tā chī le bù xīnxiān de shíwù, lā le sān tiān de dùzi, chàyìdiǎnr jiù sǐ le.
text.english: He ate stale food and had diarrhea for three days; he almost died.

text.traditional: 我差點兒忘了今天要考試，還好你告訴我，要不然這門課我一定會被當。
text.simplified: 我差点儿忘了今天要考试，还好你告诉我，要不然这门课我一定会被当。
text.pinyin: Wǒ chàdiǎnr wàngle jīntiān yào kǎoshì, háihǎo nǐ gàosu wǒ, yàobùrán zhè mén kè wǒ yídìng huì bèi dàng.
text.english: I almost forgot that I had an exam today. Good thing you told me; otherwise, I would definitely have failed this class.

summary: 差一點兒 says something almost happened.
It is followed by a verb or verb phrase, and it is usually about something the speaker did not want.

grammarPages.lessonTitleEnglish: I Want to Buy a Laptop
grammarPages.learnerPromise: Show that an action had no expected effect.
grammarPages.pattern: 白 + V (+ 了)
grammarPages.explanation: “白” should be followed by a verb, often a monosyllabic verb. It indicates an action is carried out with no effects it should have. Note when collocating with some verbs such as “吃 (eat)”, “喝 (drink)” and “住 (live)”, it means “unwilling to pay money or make effort”, e.g., “他常常來我家白吃白喝”.
grammarPages.explanationEnglish: “白” should be followed by a verb, often a monosyllabic verb. It indicates an action is carried out with no effects it should have. Note when collocating with some verbs such as “吃 (eat)”, “喝 (drink)” and “住 (live)”, it means “unwilling to pay money or make effort”, e.g., “他常常來我家白吃白喝”.
grammarPages.sourceExplanationEnglish: “白” should be followed by a verb, often a monosyllabic verb. It indicates an action is carried out with no effects it should have. Note when collocating with some verbs such as “吃 (eat)”, “喝 (drink)” and “住 (live)”, it means “unwilling to pay money or make effort”, e.g., “他常常來我家白吃白喝”.

text.traditional: 我說了這麼多次，你還是沒聽懂，真是白說了。
text.simplified: 我说了这么多次，你还是没听懂，真是白说了。
text.pinyin: Wǒ shuō le zhème duōcì, nǐ háishì méi tīngdǒng, zhēnshì bái shuō le.
text.english: I’ve said it so many times, but you still didn’t understand. It was all for nothing.

text.traditional: 那家餐廳很遠，你先打電話問他們今天做不做生意，別白跑了！
text.simplified: 那家餐厅很远，你先打电话问他们今天做不做生意，别白跑了！
text.pinyin: Nà jiā cāntīng hěn yuǎn, nǐ xiān dǎ diànhuà wèn tāmen jīntiān zuò bú zuò shēngyì, bié bái pǎo le!
text.english: That restaurant is far away. Call first to ask whether they’re open today so you don’t make the trip for nothing!

text.traditional: 我把野餐要吃的三明治都準備好了，可是朋友忽然說不去了，我白準備了。
text.simplified: 我把野餐要吃的三明治都准备好了，可是朋友忽然说不去了，我白准备了。
text.pinyin: Wǒ bǎ yěcān yào chī de sānmíngzhì dōu zhǔnbèi hǎo le, kěshì péngyǒu hūrán shuō bú qù le, wǒ bái zhǔnbèi le.
text.english: I prepared all the sandwiches for the picnic, but my friend suddenly said they weren’t going. I prepared them for nothing.

summary: 白 plus a verb, often a one-syllable one, says an action was done but did not have the effect it should have.
With verbs like 吃, 喝 and 住, it means not willing to pay money or make effort.

dialogue.title: 短文 · 去光華商場買筆電 · Going to Guanghua Digital Plaza to Buy a Laptop

text.traditional: 我在台灣沒買過 3C 產品，所以買電腦以前，我看了好幾本電腦雜誌，也問了有經驗的朋友。朋友說他總是先上網打聽哪家店比較好、哪家店打折，或是哪家店的店員比較客氣。我覺得他說得很有道理，所以前兩天我也先上網找了一家不錯的商店。
text.simplified: 我在台湾没买过 3C 产品，所以买电脑以前，我看了好几本电脑杂志，也问了有经验的朋友。朋友说他总是先上网打听哪家店比较好、哪家店打折，或是哪家店的店员比较客气。我觉得他说得很有道理，所以前两天我也先上网找了一家不错的商店。
text.pinyin: Wǒ zài Táiwān méi mǎi guò 3C chǎnpǐn, suǒyǐ mǎi diànnǎo yǐqián, wǒ kàn le hǎojǐ běn diànnǎo zázhì, yě wèn le yǒu jīngyàn de péngyǒu. Péngyǒu shuō tā zǒngshì xiān shàngwǎng dǎtīng nǎ jiā diàn bǐjiào hǎo, nǎ jiā diàn dǎzhé, huòshì nǎ jiā diàn de diànyuán bǐjiào kèqì. Wǒ juéde tā shuō de hěn yǒudàolǐ, suǒyǐ qián liǎng tiān wǒ yě xiān shàngwǎng zhǎo le yìjiā búcuò de shāngdiàn.
text.english: I had never bought any electronic product in Taiwan before, so I read several computer magazines and asked an experienced friend before buying a computer. A friend told me that he would first inquire on the Internet about which store is better, which store gives discounts, or in which store the clerks are more polite. I thought that what he said made sense, so in the past two days, I also searched for a store on the Internet.

text.traditional: 那家店在光華商場，昨天我一下課就去那裡看看。本來我想買平板，但是店員認為大學生用筆電比較方便，而且跟平板比起來，筆電還是比較好用的。
text.simplified: 那家店在光华商场，昨天我一下课就去那里看看。本来我想买平板，但是店员认为大学生用笔电比较方便，而且跟平板比起来，笔电还是比较好用的。
text.pinyin: Nà jiā diàn zài Guānghuá Shāngchǎng, zuótiān wǒ yíxià kè jiù qù nàlǐ kànkan. Běnlái wǒ xiǎng mǎi píngbǎn, dànshì diànyuán rènwéi dàxuéshēng yòng bǐdiàn bǐjiào fāngbiàn, érqiě gēn píngbǎn bǐqǐ lái, bǐdiàn háishì bǐjiào hǎoyòng de.
text.english: The store was in Guanghua Digital Plaza. I went there and had a look right after class yesterday. Originally, I wanted to buy the tablet, but the clerk thought using a laptop is more convenient for university students. Besides, in comparison to a tablet, a laptop is still more useful.

text.traditional: 店員建議我買的那部筆電是最新的產品，拿起來很輕、看起來很好用，可是價格太高了。我最近窮死了，買不起那麼貴的電腦。因為上次搬家的時候手機不見了，父母說我不愛惜東西，這兩個月不給我零用錢，逼我省錢。還好店員告訴我，那部電腦打折以後能便宜八千塊錢，而且還答應我，要是電腦有問題，不超過一年都可以免費修理，所以我當天就把電腦買回家了。付了錢以後，我差一點兒就又忘了拿自己的手機，真糊塗！
text.simplified: 店员建议我买的那部笔电是最新的产品，拿起来很轻、看起来很好用，可是价格太高了。我最近穷死了，买不起那么贵的电脑。因为上次搬家的时候手机不见了，父母说我不爱惜东西，这两个月不给我零用钱，逼我省钱。还好店员告诉我，那部电脑打折以后能便宜八千块钱，而且还答应我，要是电脑有问题，不超过一年都可以免费修理，所以我当天就把电脑买回家了。付了钱以后，我差一点儿就又忘了拿自己的手机，真糊涂！
text.pinyin: Diànyuán jiànyì wǒ mǎi de nà bù bǐdiàn shì zuìxīn de chǎnpǐn, ná qǐ lái hěn qīng, kànqǐlái hěn hǎoyòng, kěshì jiàgé tài gāo le. Wǒ zuìjìn qióng sǐ le, mǎi bù qǐ nàme guì de diànnǎo. Yīnwèi shàng cì bānjiā de shíhòu shǒujī bújiànle, fùmǔ shuō wǒ bú àixí dōngxi, zhè liǎng ge yuè bù gěi wǒ língyòngqián, bī wǒ shěngqián. Háihǎo diànyuán gàosu wǒ, nà bù diànnǎo dǎzhé yǐhòu néng piányí bāqiān kuài qián, érqiě hái dāyìng wǒ, yàoshì diànnǎo yǒu wèntí, bù chāoguò yì nián dōu kěyǐ miǎnfèi xiūlǐ, suǒyǐ wǒ dāngtiān jiù bǎ diànnǎo mǎi huí jiā le. Fù le qián yǐhòu, wǒ chàyìdiǎnr jiù yòu wàngle ná zìjǐ de shǒujī, zhēn hútú!
text.english: The laptop the clerk suggested me to buy was the newest product. It was very light to carry and looked useful, but the price was too high. I was terribly poor recently, and I couldn’t afford such an expensive computer. Because my new cell phone was gone when I was moving house last time, my parents said that I didn’t cherish my stuff, so they didn’t give me pocket money these two months in order for me to save money. Fortunately, the clerk told me later that I could save 8,000 dollars after a discount, and he also promised me that if there were problems with the computer within a year, he would definitely help me repair it for free, so I brought the computer home on that same day. After paying the money, I almost forgot my cell phone again. How clumsy I was!

text.traditional: 我很高興這次去光華商場沒白跑，很快就買到需要的筆電，省了不少麻煩。後來我又去看了其他的科技產品，有不少新發現。新產品的功能越來越多，不但能幫我們解決很多問題，也能讓我們的生活變得更便利。
text.simplified: 我很高兴这次去光华商场没白跑，很快就买到需要的笔电，省了不少麻烦。后来我又去看了其他的科技产品，有不少新发现。新产品的功能越来越多，不但能帮我们解决很多问题，也能让我们的生活变得更便利。
text.pinyin: Wǒ hěn gāoxìng zhè cì qù Guānghuá Shāngchǎng méi bái pǎo, hěn kuài jiù mǎi dào xūyào de bǐdiàn, shěng le bùshǎo máfán. Hòulái wǒ yòu qù kàn le qítā de kējì chǎnpǐn, yǒu bùshǎo xīn fāxiàn. Xīn chǎnpǐn de gōngnéng yuèláiyuè duō, búdàn néng bāng wǒmen jiějué hěn duō wèntí, yě néng ràng wǒmen de shēnghuó biàn de gèng biànlì.
text.english: I am glad that this time I didn’t go to Guanghua Digital Plaza for nothing. I quickly bought the laptop I wanted, and it saved me a lot of trouble. Afterwards I went to see other technological products and had many new discoveries. I think new products have more and more functions. They not only can help us solve many problems, but also can make our lives more convenient.

items.title: Grammar 1–3 · Fish on the Dish, Abundance Year after Year

grammarPages.lessonTitleEnglish: Fish on the Dish, Abundance Year after Year
grammarPages.titleTraditional: 想起來：想起來了／沒想起來／想得起來／想不起來
grammarPages.titleEnglish: Now Remember / Can or Can’t Remember
grammarPages.learnerPromise: Recall something you nearly forgot.
grammarPages.explanation: “想起來” is used when someone suddenly remembers something that is almost forgotten or recalls something with great effort. “想得起來／想不起來” indicates whether or not someone can remember something almost forgotten or happened a long time ago.
grammarPages.explanationEnglish: “想起來” is used when someone suddenly remembers something that is almost forgotten or recalls something with great effort. “想得起來／想不起來” indicates whether or not someone can remember something almost forgotten or happened a long time ago.
grammarPages.sourceExplanationEnglish: “想起來” is used when someone suddenly remembers something that is almost forgotten or recalls something with great effort. “想得起來／想不起來” indicates whether or not someone can remember something almost forgotten or happened a long time ago.
grammarPages.pattern: 想起來了／沒想起來／想得起來／想不起來

text.traditional: 太太：你怎麼看起來這麼緊張啊？先生：我忽然想起來今天要開會，我得快點兒去公司！
text.simplified: 太太：你怎么看起来这么紧张啊？先生：我忽然想起来今天要开会，我得快点儿去公司！
text.pinyin: Tàitai: Nǐ zěnme kànqǐlái zhème jǐnzhāng a? Xiānshēng: Wǒ hūrán xiǎng qǐlái jīntiān yào kāihuì, wǒ děi kuài diǎnr qù gōngsī!
text.english: Wife: Why do you look so nervous? Husband: I suddenly remembered that I have a meeting today. I have to hurry to the office!

text.traditional: A：你記得我們上次去的 KTV 在哪裡嗎？B：我想想……想起來了！就在捷運龍山寺站的附近。
text.simplified: A：你记得我们上次去的 KTV 在哪里吗？B：我想想……想起来了！就在捷运龙山寺站的附近。
text.pinyin: A: Nǐ jìde wǒmen shàng cì qù de KTV zài nǎlǐ ma? B: Wǒ xiǎng xiǎng… xiǎng qǐlái le! Jiù zài Jiéyùn Lóngshān Sì Zhàn de fùjìn.
text.english: A: Do you remember where the KTV we went to last time is? B: Let me think… I remember now! It’s right near Longshan Temple MRT Station.

text.traditional: A：我是你的小學同學，你還記得我的名字嗎？B：你叫……對不起，我想不起來了。
text.simplified: A：我是你的小学同学，你还记得我的名字吗？B：你叫……对不起，我想不起来了。
text.pinyin: A: Wǒ shì nǐ de xiǎoxué tóngxué, nǐ hái jìde wǒ de míngzi ma? B: Nǐ jiào… duìbùqǐ, wǒ xiǎng bù qǐlái le.
text.english: A: I am your elementary school classmate. Do you still remember my name? B: Your name is… Sorry, I can’t remember.

text.traditional: A：你小時候第一次看的卡通是什麼，你想得起來嗎？B：那麼久以前的事，我怎麼想得起來！
text.simplified: A：你小时候第一次看的卡通是什么，你想得起来吗？B：那么久以前的事，我怎么想得起来！
text.pinyin: A: Nǐ xiǎoshíhòu dì yī cì kàn de kǎtōng shì shénme, nǐ xiǎng de qǐlái ma? B: Nàme jiǔ yǐqián de shì, wǒ zěnme xiǎng de qǐlái!
text.english: A: What was the first cartoon you watched as a child? Can you remember? B: How could I remember something from so long ago!

grammarPages.exercisePreview: Use 想起來 to complete the four prompts.
grammarPages.exerciseInstruction: Complete the sentences with a suitable 想起來 form.
summary: 想起來 is used when someone suddenly remembers something almost forgotten, or remembers it with great effort.
想得起來 and 想不起來 say whether someone can remember something almost forgotten or from long ago.

grammarPages.lessonTitleEnglish: Fish on the Dish, Abundance Year after Year
grammarPages.learnerPromise: Say what you have never done with 從來沒, or what you never do with 從來不.
grammarPages.explanation: This pattern expresses that someone has never done something, or never does something.
grammarPages.explanationEnglish: This pattern expresses that someone has never done something, or never does something.
grammarPages.sourceExplanationEnglish: This pattern expresses that someone has never done something, or never does something.
grammarPages.pattern: 從來 + 沒／不 + V

text.traditional: A：這個週末我們一起去 KTV 唱歌，怎麼樣？B：太好了！我從來沒去過 KTV，一定很好玩。
text.simplified: A：这个周末我们一起去 KTV 唱歌，怎么样？B：太好了！我从来没去过 KTV，一定很好玩。
text.pinyin: A: Zhège zhōumò wǒmen yìqǐ qù KTV chànggē, zěnmeyàng? B: Tài hǎo le! Wǒ cónglái méi qù guo KTV, yídìng hěn hǎowán.
text.english: A: How about going to KTV to sing together this weekend? B: Great! I’ve never been to KTV; it must be fun.

text.traditional: A：下班以後，我們找老王一起去健身吧！B：不用找他了，他從來不運動！
text.simplified: A：下班以后，我们找老王一起去健身吧！B：不用找他了，他从来不运动！
text.pinyin: A: Xiàbān yǐhòu, wǒmen zhǎo Lǎo Wáng yìqǐ qù jiànshēn ba! B: Búyòng zhǎo tā le, tā cónglái bú yùndòng!
text.english: A: Let’s ask Lao Wang to work out with us after work! B: There’s no need; he never exercises!

text.traditional: A：我從來沒去過阿里山，聽說那裡的日出很美，是真的嗎？B：阿里山的日出是很美，夜裡看星星也不錯喔！
text.simplified: A：我从来没去过阿里山，听说那里的日出很美，是真的吗？B：阿里山的日出是很美，夜里看星星也不错喔！
text.pinyin: A: Wǒ cónglái méi qù guo Ālǐ Shān, tīngshuō nàlǐ de rìchū hěn měi, shì zhēnde ma? B: Ālǐ Shān de rìchū shì hěn měi, yèlǐ kàn xīngxīng yě búcuò o!
text.english: A: I’ve never been to Alishan. I heard the sunrise there is beautiful. Is that true? B: The sunrise at Alishan is beautiful, and stargazing at night is nice too!

grammarPages.exercisePreview: Complete the dialogues with 從來＋沒／不.
summary: 從來 plus 沒 or 不 says someone has never done something, or never does it.
Put 從來 and 沒 or 不 before the verb.

grammarPages.lessonTitleEnglish: Fish on the Dish, Abundance Year after Year
grammarPages.learnerPromise: Add 等等 after a list when more examples of the same kind are left unlisted.
grammarPages.explanation: Similar to “等”, “等等” is used to show there are still more items of the same kind that are not entirely listed. Normally, “等等” should not be placed after proper nouns.
grammarPages.explanationEnglish: Similar to “等”, “等等” is used to show there are still more items of the same kind that are not entirely listed. Normally, “等等” should not be placed after proper nouns.
grammarPages.sourceExplanationEnglish: Similar to “等”, “等等” is used to show there are still more items of the same kind that are not entirely listed. Normally, “等等” should not be placed after proper nouns.
grammarPages.pattern: Examples + 等等

text.traditional: 便利商店的貼紙，可以換尺、牙刷、卡通娃娃等等。
text.simplified: 便利商店的贴纸，可以换尺、牙刷、卡通娃娃等等。
text.pinyin: Biànlì shāngdiàn de tiēzhǐ, kěyǐ huàn chǐ, yáshuā, kǎtōng wáwa děngděng.
text.english: Convenience store stickers can be exchanged for rulers, toothbrushes, cartoon dolls, and so on.

text.traditional: 為了身體健康，薯條、漢堡、餅乾等等，最好少吃。
text.simplified: 为了身体健康，薯条、汉堡、饼干等等，最好少吃。
text.pinyin: Wèile shēntǐ jiànkāng, shǔtiáo, hànbǎo, bǐnggān děngděng, zuìhǎo shǎo chī.
text.english: For good health, it’s best to eat fewer french fries, hamburgers, cookies, and similar foods.

text.traditional: 去鄉下爺爺奶奶家的時候，我會幫他們種花、剪草等等。
text.simplified: 去乡下爷爷奶奶家的时候，我会帮他们种花、剪草等等。
text.pinyin: Qù xiāngxià yéye nǎinai jiā de shíhòu, wǒ huì bāng tāmen zhòng huā, jiǎn cǎo děngděng.
text.english: When I go to my grandparents’ home in the countryside, I help them plant flowers, cut grass, and so on.

grammarPages.exercisePreview: Complete the dialogues with 等等.
grammarPages.exerciseInstruction: Complete the dialogues with 等等.
summary: 等等 at the end of a list shows there are more items of the same kind that are not listed.
It works like 等. Normally, don't put 等等 after proper nouns.

dialogue.title: 年年有「魚」
dialogue.setting: 在學校餐廳 · In the school canteen
grammarFocus: 想起來：想起來了／沒想起來／想得起來／想不起來

text.traditional: （在學校餐廳）
text.simplified: （在学校餐厅）
text.pinyin: (Zài xuéxiào cāntīng)
text.english: (In the school canteen.)

text.traditional: 老師對報告的要求真多，所以我的期末報告修改了好幾次，還好最後都完成了，可以開心地放寒假了！
text.simplified: 老师对报告的要求真多，所以我的期末报告修改了好几次，还好最后都完成了，可以开心地放寒假了！
text.pinyin: Lǎoshī duì bàogào de yāoqiú zhēn duō, suǒyǐ wǒ de qímò bàogào xiūgǎi le hǎojǐ cì, háihǎo zuìhòu dōu wánchéng le, kěyǐ kāixīn de fàng hánjià le!
text.english: The teacher had many requirements for our reports, so I revised my final report many times. Fortunately, I’ve got everything done at last. I can happily enjoy the winter vacation!

text.traditional: 是啊！我一回去就要幫媽媽打掃，準備過年。
text.simplified: 是啊！我一回去就要帮妈妈打扫，准备过年。
text.pinyin: Shì a! Wǒ yì huíqù jiùyào bāng māma dǎsǎo, zhǔnbèi guònián.
text.english: Right! As soon as I go back home, I will help my mom do the cleaning and prepare for the coming New Year.

text.traditional: 過年？我想起來了，是不是中國新年？
text.simplified: 过年？我想起来了，是不是中国新年？
text.pinyin: Guònián? Wǒ xiǎng qǐlái le, shì bú shì Zhōngguó xīnnián?
text.english: New Year? I remember! Is it the Chinese New Year?

text.traditional: 對，就是中國新年，也叫春節。義大利人不過年嗎？
text.simplified: 对，就是中国新年，也叫春节。义大利人不过年吗？
text.pinyin: Duì, jiùshì Zhōngguó xīnnián, yě jiào Chūnjié. Yìdàlì rén búguò nián ma?
text.english: Yes, it is exactly the Chinese New Year, also called the Spring Festival. Don’t the Italians celebrate the New Year?

text.traditional: 我們過的是一月一號的新年。十二月三十一號跨年那天，熱鬧極了。
text.simplified: 我们过的是一月一号的新年。十二月三十一号跨年那天，热闹极了。
text.pinyin: Wǒmen guò de shì yī yuè yī hào de xīnnián. Shí'èr yuè sānshí yī hào kuànián nà tiān, rènao jíle.
text.english: We celebrate it on January 1st. On December 31st, New Year’s Eve, it is extremely lively.

text.traditional: 原來是這樣。不過，你知道中國人是怎麼過年的嗎？
text.simplified: 原来是这样。不过，你知道中国人是怎么过年的吗？
text.pinyin: Yuánlái shì zhèyàng. Búguò, nǐ zhīdào Zhōngguó rén shì zěnme guònián de ma?
text.english: Oh, I see. But do you know how Chinese people celebrate the New Year?

text.traditional: 從來沒聽過……妳們給我介紹一下吧！
text.simplified: 从来没听过……你们给我介绍一下吧！
text.pinyin: Cónglái méi tīng guo… nǐ men gěi wǒ jièshào yíxià ba!
text.english: I’ve never heard about it... Please give me a short introduction!

text.traditional: 春節的前一天是「除夕」，除夕前幾天，得把房子打掃乾淨……
text.simplified: 春节的前一天是「除夕」，除夕前几天，得把房子打扫干净……
text.pinyin: Chūnjié de qián yì tiān shì “Chúxī”, chúxī qián jǐ tiān, děi bǎ fángzi dǎsǎo gānjìng…
text.english: The day before the Spring Festival is Chinese New Year’s Eve. A few days before the Chinese New Year’s Eve, we need to clean up the house…

text.traditional: （美心接著說）除夕那天下午，我們回到爺爺、奶奶家以後，要先拜拜；等拜完了祖先，家人就聚在一起吃「年夜飯」。
text.simplified: （美心接着说）除夕那天下午，我们回到爷爷、奶奶家以后，要先拜拜；等拜完了祖先，家人就聚在一起吃「年夜饭」。
text.pinyin: (Měixīn jiēzhe shuō) Chúxī nà tiān xiàwǔ, wǒmen huí dào yéye, nǎinai jiā yǐhòu, yào xiān bàibài; děng bài wán le zǔxiān, jiārén jiù jù zài yìqǐ chī “niányèfàn”.
text.english: (Continues to speak.) On the afternoon of Chinese New Year’s Eve, after we return to grandpa and grandma’s house, we worship together first. After worshiping the ancestors, the whole family gathers to eat “family reunion dinner” together.

text.traditional: 年夜飯跟平常吃的飯不一樣嗎？
text.simplified: 年夜饭跟平常吃的饭不一样吗？
text.pinyin: Niányèfàn gēn píngcháng chī de fàn bù yíyàng ma?
text.english: Is the family reunion dinner different from usual food?

text.traditional: 年夜飯特別豐富喔！我媽媽會炸年糕、煮水餃、炒米粉，還會煎一條好吃的魚，可是不能吃完。
text.simplified: 年夜饭特别丰富喔！我妈妈会炸年糕、煮水饺、炒米粉，还会煎一条好吃的鱼，可是不能吃完。
text.pinyin: Niányèfàn tèbié fēngfù o! Wǒ māma huì zhà niángāo, zhǔ shuǐjiǎo, chǎo mǐfěn, hái huì jiān yì tiáo hǎochī de yú, kěshì bùnéng chī wán.
text.english: The family reunion dinner is particularly abundant! My mom will make deep-fried glutinous rice cake, boiled dumplings, and fried rice noodles along with a delicious fried fish. However, we can’t eat up the whole fish.

text.traditional: 為什麼不能吃完？
text.simplified: 为什么不能吃完？
text.pinyin: Wèishénme bùnéng chī wán?
text.english: Why can’t you eat it up?

text.traditional: 因為要「年年有餘」，「餘」跟「魚」都唸 yú，有「剩下」的意思。如果年夜飯有剩下的魚，新的一年就會有很多食物。
text.simplified: 因为要「年年有余」，「余」跟「鱼」都念 yú，有「剩下」的意思。如果年夜饭有剩下的鱼，新的一年就会有很多食物。
text.pinyin: Yīnwèi yào “niánnián yǒuyú”, “yú” gēn “yú” dōu niàn yú, yǒu “shèngxià” de yìsi. Rúguǒ niányèfàn yǒu shèngxià de yú, xīn de yì nián jiù huì yǒu hěn duō shíwù.
text.english: Because we hope to have a prosperous new year! Both “餘” and “魚” are both pronounced as yú. It means “surplus”. If there’s some fish left during the dinner, we’ll have plenty of food in the coming new year!

text.traditional: 除了魚，像年糕、發糕、蘿蔔糕等等，也是過年會吃的食物。
text.simplified: 除了鱼，像年糕、发糕、萝卜糕等等，也是过年会吃的食物。
text.pinyin: Chúle yú, xiàng niángāo, fāgāo, luóbogāo děngděng, yě shì guònián huì chī de shíwù.
text.english: Apart from fish, things like glutinous rice cakes, sponge cakes, radish cakes, and so on are also eaten during the Chinese New Year.

text.traditional: 這些東西也有特別的意思嗎？
text.simplified: 这些东西也有特别的意思吗？
text.pinyin: Zhèxiē dōngxi yě yǒu tèbié de yìsi ma?
text.english: Do these things have special meanings, too?

text.traditional: 有啊！年糕代表「年年高升」、發糕是「發財」的意思；吃了蘿蔔糕就會很幸運喔！
text.simplified: 有啊！年糕代表「年年高升」、发糕是「发财」的意思；吃了萝卜糕就会很幸运喔！
text.pinyin: Yǒu a! Niángāo dàibiǎo “niánnián gāoshēng”, fāgāo shì “fācái” de yìsi; chī le luóbogāo jiù huì hěn xìngyùn o!
text.english: They do! Glutinous rice cake represents getting promoted year by year, sponge cake means making a fortune, and you will be lucky when you eat the radish cake!

text.traditional: 還要準備「平平安安」的蘋果跟「大吉大利」的橘子。
text.simplified: 还要准备「平平安安」的苹果跟「大吉大利」的橘子。
text.pinyin: Háiyào zhǔnbèi “píngpíng ān'ān” de píngguǒ gēn “dàjídàlì” de júzi.
text.english: Also, we still have apples symbolizing peace, and tangerines symbolizing great fortune and great favor.

text.traditional: 我了解了，真是又特別又豐富的大餐！
text.simplified: 我了解了，真是又特别又丰富的大餐！
text.pinyin: Wǒ liǎojiě le, zhēnshì yòu tèbié yòu fēngfù de dà cān!
text.english: I get it. It is really a special and abundant meal!

text.traditional: 如果你跟我去爺爺奶奶家過年，今年的除夕就更加熱鬧了！
text.simplified: 如果你跟我去爷爷奶奶家过年，今年的除夕就更加热闹了！
text.pinyin: Rúguǒ nǐ gēn wǒ qù yéye nǎinai jiā guònián, jīnnián de chúxī jiù gèngjiā rènao le!
text.english: If you go to my grandparents’ house with me, this Chinese New Year’s Eve will be even more lively!

text.traditional: （這個時候，以凡的手機響了，是媽媽寄給他的一封電子郵件，他看完以後很難過。）
text.simplified: （这个时候，以凡的手机响了，是妈妈寄给他的一封电子邮件，他看完以后很难过。）
text.pinyin: (Zhège shíhòu, Yǐfán de shǒujī xiǎng le, shì māma jì gěi tā de yì fēng diànzǐ yóujiàn, tā kàn wán yǐhòu hěn nánguò.)
text.english: (At that moment Yifan’s cellphone rang. It was his mom sending him an email. He was very sad after reading it.)

text.traditional: 我媽媽說，她訂不到機票，寒假不能來看我了。
text.simplified: 我妈妈说，她订不到机票，寒假不能来看我了。
text.pinyin: Wǒ māma shuō, tā dìng búdào jīpiào, hánjià bùnéng lái kàn wǒ le.
text.english: My mom said that she couldn’t book the ticket so that she couldn’t come to see me during winter vacation.

text.traditional: 沒關係，等過完年，我帶你去找我舅舅、舅媽，他們很親切，而且舅媽會做義大利麵，你可以吃吃看。
text.simplified: 没关系，等过完年，我带你去找我舅舅、舅妈，他们很亲切，而且舅妈会做义大利面，你可以吃吃看。
text.pinyin: Méiguānxi, děng guò wán nián, wǒ dài nǐ qù zhǎo wǒ jiùjiu, jiùmā, tāmen hěn qīnqiè, érqiě jiùmā huì zuò Yìdàlì miàn, nǐ kěyǐ chīchi kàn.
text.english: It’s ok. After the Chinese New Year, I’ll take you to visit my uncle and aunt. They are very kind to people. Besides, my aunt can make pasta. You can try it.

text.traditional: （心裡感覺相當溫暖）好啊！太感謝妳了！
text.simplified: （心里感觉相当温暖）好啊！太感谢你了！
text.pinyin: (Xīnlǐ gǎnjué xiāngdāng wēnnuǎn) Hǎo a! Tài gǎnxiè nǐ le!
text.english: (Feels quite warm inside.) Alright! Thank you so much!

text.traditional: 對了！元宵節那天，我可以帶你去看燈會，有的燈籠上面還畫了十二生肖。
text.simplified: 对了！元宵节那天，我可以带你去看灯会，有的灯笼上面还画了十二生肖。
text.pinyin: Duìle! Yuánxiāojié nà tiān, wǒ kěyǐ dài nǐ qù kàn dēnghuì, yǒude dēnglóng shàngmiàn hái huà le shí'èr shēngxiào.
text.english: Oh! On Lantern Festival, I can take you to the lantern show. There are also zodiac paintings on some of the lanterns.

text.traditional: 十二生肖？
text.simplified: 十二生肖？
text.pinyin: Shí'èr shēngxiào?
text.english: Zodiac?

text.traditional: 對啊！就是鼠、牛、虎、兔、龍、蛇、馬、羊、猴、雞、狗、豬。
text.simplified: 对啊！就是鼠、牛、虎、兔、龙、蛇、马、羊、猴、鸡、狗、猪。
text.pinyin: Duì a! Jiùshì shǔ, niú, hǔ, tù, lóng, shé, mǎ, yáng, hóu, jī, gǒu, zhū.
text.english: Right! It is the mouse, the cow, the tiger, the rabbit, the dragon, the snake, the horse, the sheep, the monkey, the chicken, the dog, and the pig.

text.traditional: 妳說了這麼多動物，怎麼沒有貓呢？
text.simplified: 你说了这么多动物，怎么没有猫呢？
text.pinyin: Nǐ shuō le zhème duō dòngwù, zěnme méiyǒu māo ne?
text.english: You mentioned so many animals. Why are there no cats?

text.traditional: 有空我們再告訴你十二生肖的故事。你不知道我是屬虎的吧？
text.simplified: 有空我们再告诉你十二生肖的故事。你不知道我是属虎的吧？
text.pinyin: Yǒukòng wǒmen zài gàosu nǐ shí'èr shēngxiào de gùshì. Nǐ bù zhīdào wǒ shì shǔ hǔ de ba?
text.english: When we have time, we will tell you the story of the zodiac. You don’t know that I was born in the year of the tiger?

text.traditional: 是嗎？難怪妳那麼愛生氣！
text.simplified: 是吗？难怪你那么爱生气！
text.pinyin: Shì ma? Nánguài nǐ nàme ài shēngqì!
text.english: Were you? No wonder you enjoy getting angry so much!

text.traditional: 哈哈哈……
text.simplified: 哈哈哈……
text.pinyin: Hāhāhā…
text.english: Hahaha...

items.title: Grammar 4–8 · Here Comes the “Nian”

grammarPages.lessonTitleEnglish: Fish on the Dish, Abundance Year after Year
grammarPages.learnerPromise: Link a situation with the result that follows right away.
grammarPages.explanation: This pattern indicates when a situation occurs, another situation ensues right away. In this pattern, “當” is often followed by “……的時候”.
grammarPages.explanationEnglish: This pattern indicates when a situation occurs, another situation ensues right away. In this pattern, “當” is often followed by “……的時候”.
grammarPages.sourceExplanationEnglish: This pattern indicates when a situation occurs, another situation ensues right away. In this pattern, “當” is often followed by “……的時候”.
grammarPages.pattern: 當 + situation（+ 的時候），就 + result

text.traditional: 當警察一出現，小偷就趕快跑了。
text.simplified: 当警察一出现，小偷就赶快跑了。
text.pinyin: Dāng jǐngchá yì chūxiàn, xiǎotōu jiù gǎnkuài pǎo le.
text.english: As soon as the police appeared, the thief ran away quickly.

text.traditional: 當你覺得難過、生氣的時候，就應該去操場運動一下。
text.simplified: 当你觉得难过、生气的时候，就应该去操场运动一下。
text.pinyin: Dāng nǐ juéde nánguò, shēngqì de shíhòu, jiù yīnggāi qù cāochǎng yùndòng yíxià.
text.english: When you feel sad or angry, you should go exercise on the sports field.

text.traditional: 當莫以凡第一天參加功夫社的時候，就愛上了中國功夫。
text.simplified: 当莫以凡第一天参加功夫社的时候，就爱上了中国功夫。
text.pinyin: Dāng Mò Yǐfán dìyī tiān cānjiā gōngfu shè de shíhòu, jiù àishàng le Zhōngguó gōngfu.
text.english: On his very first day at the kungfu club, Mo Yifan fell in love with Chinese kungfu.

grammarPages.exercisePreview: Complete the dialogues with 當……，就…….
grammarPages.exerciseInstruction: Answer each question with 當……，就…….
summary: 當 ... 就 says that when one situation happens, another follows right away.
當 is often used with 的時候.

grammarPages.lessonTitleEnglish: Fish on the Dish, Abundance Year after Year
grammarPages.learnerPromise: Use 讓 as a passive marker or as a verb meaning cause, allow, or let.
grammarPages.explanation: 1. Used as Preposition: S＋讓＋NP（＋給）＋V了 This pattern functions as the passive voice expression. The usage of “讓” here is similar to “被”; however, the Agent after “被” can be omitted while after “讓” cannot be. 2. Used as Verb: (1) to make someone ..., to cause something to happen (2) to allow, to permit someone to do something (3) to let someone do something or to have someone do something: This usage of imperative “讓” is more polite and euphemistic.
grammarPages.explanationEnglish: 1. Used as Preposition: S＋讓＋NP（＋給）＋V了 This pattern functions as the passive voice expression. The usage of “讓” here is similar to “被”; however, the Agent after “被” can be omitted while after “讓” cannot be. 2. Used as Verb: (1) to make someone ..., to cause something to happen (2) to allow, to permit someone to do something (3) to let someone do something or to have someone do something: This usage of imperative “讓” is more polite and euphemistic.
grammarPages.sourceExplanationEnglish: 1. Used as Preposition: S＋讓＋NP（＋給）＋V了 This pattern functions as the passive voice expression. The usage of “讓” here is similar to “被”; however, the Agent after “被” can be omitted while after “讓” cannot be. 2. Used as Verb: (1) to make someone ..., to cause something to happen (2) to allow, to permit someone to do something (3) to let someone do something or to have someone do something: This usage of imperative “讓” is more polite and euphemistic.
grammarPages.pattern: S + 讓 + NP（+ 給）+ V了

text.traditional: 李先生剛買的照相機讓同事（給）弄壞了。
text.simplified: 李先生刚买的照相机让同事（给）弄坏了。
text.pinyin: Lǐ xiānshēng gāng mǎi de zhàoxiàngjī ràng tóngshì (gěi) nòng huài le.
text.english: The camera Mr. Li just bought was broken by a coworker.

text.traditional: 每次跟朋友去 KTV 唱歌，都讓他非常開心。
text.simplified: 每次跟朋友去 KTV 唱歌，都让他非常开心。
text.pinyin: Měicì gēn péngyǒu qù KTV chànggē, dōu ràng tā fēicháng kāixīn.
text.english: Every time he goes to KTV to sing with friends, it makes him very happy.

text.traditional: 我不舒服，老師讓我早一點兒回家休息。
text.simplified: 我不舒服，老师让我早一点儿回家休息。
text.pinyin: Wǒ bù shūfu, lǎoshī ràng wǒ zǎo yìdiǎnr huí jiā xiūxí.
text.english: I didn’t feel well, so the teacher let me go home early to rest.

text.traditional: 媽媽讓孩子把臥室打掃好了以後，才能玩遊戲。
text.simplified: 妈妈让孩子把卧室打扫好了以后，才能玩游戏。
text.pinyin: Māma ràng háizi bǎ wòshì dǎsǎo hǎo le yǐhòu, cáinéng wán yóuxì.
text.english: Mom had the child finish cleaning the bedroom first; only then could the child play games.

text.traditional: 老闆讓我留下來把筆電修好，才讓我下班。這件事讓我很生氣。
text.simplified: 老板让我留下来把笔电修好，才让我下班。这件事让我很生气。
text.pinyin: Lǎobǎn ràng wǒ liú xià lái bǎ bǐdiàn xiū hǎo, cái ràng wǒ xiàbān. Zhè jiàn shì ràng wǒ hěn shēngqì.
text.english: The boss made me stay and fix the laptop, and only then let me leave work. This made me very angry.

subsections.title: Used as Preposition
subsections.explanation: This pattern functions as the passive voice expression. The usage of “讓” here is similar to “被”; however, the Agent after “被” can be omitted while after “讓” cannot be.
subsections.pattern: S + 讓 + NP（+ 給）+ V了

subsections.title: Used as Verb
subsections.explanation:
(1) to make someone ..., to cause something to happen
(2) to allow, to permit someone to do something
(3) to let someone do something or to have someone do something: This usage of imperative “讓” is more polite and euphemistic.

summary: 讓 can work like 被, to say what was done to the subject. The doer after 讓 can't be left out.
As a verb, 讓 can mean to cause something to happen, or to make someone feel or do something.
It can also mean to allow someone to do something. Asking someone to do something with 讓 sounds more polite and soft.

grammarPages.lessonTitleEnglish: Fish on the Dish, Abundance Year after Year
grammarPages.learnerPromise: Say that a choice or situation does not matter to someone.
grammarPages.explanation: This pattern is often placed after the things the speaker feels indifferent to or does not care about. It can also be used independently.
grammarPages.explanationEnglish: This pattern is often placed after the things the speaker feels indifferent to or does not care about. It can also be used independently.
grammarPages.sourceExplanationEnglish: This pattern is often placed after the things the speaker feels indifferent to or does not care about. It can also be used independently.
grammarPages.pattern: (Thing) + 無所謂

text.traditional: 父母覺得孩子胖或是瘦都無所謂，只要健康就好了。
text.simplified: 父母觉得孩子胖或是瘦都无所谓，只要健康就好了。
text.pinyin: Fùmǔ juéde háizi pàng huòshì shòu dōu wúsuǒwèi, zhǐyào jiànkāng jiù hǎo le.
text.english: The parents don’t mind whether their child is fat or thin, as long as the child is healthy.

text.traditional: 太太：這個週末我們要去哪裡玩？先生：妳決定吧！我無所謂。
text.simplified: 太太：这个周末我们要去哪里玩？先生：你决定吧！我无所谓。
text.pinyin: Tàitai: Zhège zhōumò wǒmen yào qù nǎlǐ wán? Xiānshēng: Nǐ juédìng ba! Wǒ wúsuǒwèi.
text.english: Wife: Where should we go this weekend? Husband: You decide! I don’t mind.

text.traditional: 老闆：歡迎你來我的餐廳打工，可是錢不多，你願意嗎？學生：錢多不多無所謂，只要能得到寶貴的經驗就好了。
text.simplified: 老板：欢迎你来我的餐厅打工，可是钱不多，你愿意吗？学生：钱多不多无所谓，只要能得到宝贵的经验就好了。
text.pinyin: Lǎobǎn: Huānyíng nǐ lái wǒ de cāntīng dǎgōng, kěshì qián bù duō, nǐ yuànyì ma? Xuéshēng: Qián duō bù duō wúsuǒwèi, zhǐyào néng dédào bǎoguì de jīngyàn jiù hǎo le.
text.english: Boss: Welcome to work at my restaurant, but the pay is low. Are you willing? Student: Whether the pay is high or low doesn’t matter, as long as I can gain valuable experience.

grammarPages.exercisePreview: Complete each response with 無所謂.
summary: 無所謂 shows the speaker is indifferent to something or does not care about it.
Put it after the thing, or use it alone.

grammarPages.lessonTitleEnglish: Fish on the Dish, Abundance Year after Year
grammarPages.learnerPromise: Use 走 after a verb to show that something leaves or disappears, or that an action can or cannot make it leave.
grammarPages.explanation: In this pattern, V can be action verbs, such as “搬（move）”, “拿（take）”, “帶（bring）”, “跑（run）”, “趕（drive）”, “嚇（scare）”, etc. “走” means “to go” or “to leave”. The “走” after the verb, used as post verb complement, means to leave or to disappear.
grammarPages.explanationEnglish: In this pattern, V can be action verbs, such as “搬（move）”, “拿（take）”, “帶（bring）”, “跑（run）”, “趕（drive）”, “嚇（scare）”, etc. “走” means “to go” or “to leave”. The “走” after the verb, used as post verb complement, means to leave or to disappear.
grammarPages.sourceExplanationEnglish: In this pattern, V can be action verbs, such as “搬（move）”, “拿（take）”, “帶（bring）”, “跑（run）”, “趕（drive）”, “嚇（scare）”, etc. “走” means “to go” or “to leave”. The “走” after the verb, used as post verb complement, means to leave or to disappear.
grammarPages.pattern: V + 走了／沒 + V + 走／V + 得走／V + 不走

text.traditional: 你們說話的聲音太大了，把孩子們都嚇走了。
text.simplified: 你们说话的声音太大了，把孩子们都吓走了。
text.pinyin: Nǐmen shuōhuà de shēngyīn tài dà le, bǎ háizi men dōu xià zǒu le.
text.english: Your voices were so loud that you scared the children away.

text.traditional: 良介已經不住在宿舍了，他上個學期末就搬走了。
text.simplified: 良介已经不住在宿舍了，他上个学期末就搬走了。
text.pinyin: Liángjiè yǐjīng bú zhù zài sùshè le, tā shàng ge xuéqí mò jiù bān zǒu le.
text.english: Ryosuke no longer lives in the dorm; he moved out at the end of last semester.

text.traditional: 這些小說是她要送給同學的，所以回國的時候沒帶走。
text.simplified: 这些小说是她要送给同学的，所以回国的时候没带走。
text.pinyin: Zhèxiē xiǎoshuō shì tā yào sòng gěi tóngxué de, suǒyǐ huíguó de shíhòu méi dài zǒu.
text.english: These novels are for her classmates, so she didn’t take them with her when she returned home.

text.traditional: 把錢存在銀行很安全，誰偷得走呢？
text.simplified: 把钱存在银行很安全，谁偷得走呢？
text.pinyin: Bǎ qián cúnzài yínháng hěn ānquán, shéi tōu de zǒu ne?
text.english: It’s safe to keep money in the bank. Who could steal it?

text.traditional: 有一隻蟲子飛進我的房間裡，怎麼趕都趕不走。
text.simplified: 有一只虫子飞进我的房间里，怎么赶都赶不走。
text.pinyin: Yǒu yì zhī chóngzi fēi jìn wǒ de fángjiān lǐ, zěnme gǎn dōu gǎn bù zǒu.
text.english: A bug flew into my room, and no matter how I shoo it, I can’t get it to leave.

summary: 走 after an action verb means something leaves or disappears.
The verb is an action verb, such as 搬, 拿 or 帶.
Put 得 or 不 between the verb and 走 to say you can or can't.

grammarPages.lessonTitleEnglish: Fish on the Dish, Abundance Year after Year
grammarPages.learnerPromise: Name an accomplished fact that prevented a different situation from happening.
grammarPages.explanation: “要不是” is followed by an accomplished fact. Without the fact, a following situation would occur. That is, the following situation did not really occur.
grammarPages.explanationEnglish: “要不是” is followed by an accomplished fact. Without the fact, a following situation would occur. That is, the following situation did not really occur.
grammarPages.sourceExplanationEnglish: “要不是” is followed by an accomplished fact. Without the fact, a following situation would occur. That is, the following situation did not really occur.
grammarPages.pattern: 要不是 + accomplished fact，result that would otherwise occur

text.traditional: 要不是春假去了阿里山，我就看不到那麼美麗的日出了。
text.simplified: 要不是春假去了阿里山，我就看不到那么美丽的日出了。
text.pinyin: Yàobúshì chūnjià qù le Ālǐ Shān, wǒ jiù kàn búdào nàme měilì de rìchū le.
text.english: If I hadn’t gone to Alishan during spring break, I wouldn’t have seen such a beautiful sunrise.

text.traditional: 要不是去同學家過年，莫以凡一個人在宿舍一定會很無聊的。
text.simplified: 要不是去同学家过年，莫以凡一个人在宿舍一定会很无聊的。
text.pinyin: Yàobúshì qù tóngxué jiā guònián, Mò Yǐfán yígerén zài sùshè yídìng huì hěn wúliáo de.
text.english: If he hadn’t gone to a classmate’s home for New Year, Mo Yifan would have been very bored alone in the dorm.

text.traditional: 要不是住過民宿，我就不知道有些民宿比飯店更舒服呢！
text.simplified: 要不是住过民宿，我就不知道有些民宿比饭店更舒服呢！
text.pinyin: Yàobúshì zhù guo mínsù, wǒ jiù bù zhīdào yǒuxiē mínsù bǐ fàndiàn gèng shūfu ne!
text.english: If I hadn’t stayed at a homestay, I wouldn’t know that some homestays are more comfortable than hotels!

grammarPages.exercisePreview: Complete the dialogues with 要不是.
grammarPages.exerciseInstruction: Complete the dialogues with 要不是.
summary: 要不是 is followed by a fact that did happen. Without that fact, something else would have happened.
The second situation did not really happen.

text.traditional: 從前，有一隻住在海裡的怪獸，名字叫「年」。從一月到十二月，「年」都在睡覺，什麼東西都不吃。到了除夕，當天一黑，「年」就會出來找東西吃。雞、鴨、人等動物，「年」都吃，讓大家非常害怕，不能好好地過日子，只好帶著一些食物，趕快跑到山上去。
text.simplified: 从前，有一只住在海里的怪兽，名字叫「年」。从一月到十二月，「年」都在睡觉，什么东西都不吃。到了除夕，当天一黑，「年」就会出来找东西吃。鸡、鸭、人等动物，「年」都吃，让大家非常害怕，不能好好地过日子，只好带着一些食物，赶快跑到山上去。
text.pinyin: Cóngqián, yǒu yì zhī zhù zài hǎi lǐ de guàishòu, míngzi jiào “nián”. Cóng yī yuè dào shí'èr yuè, “nián” dōu zài shuìjiào, shénme dōngxi dōu bù chī. Dào le chúxī, dāngtiān yì hēi, “nián” jiù huì chūlái zhǎo dōngxi chī. Jī, yā, rén děng dòngwù, “nián” dōu chī, ràng dàjiā fēicháng hàipà, bùnéng hǎohǎo de guòrìzi, zhǐhǎo dài zhe yìxiē shíwù, gǎnkuài pǎo dào shān shàngqù.
text.english: Once upon a time, there was a monster living in the sea. It was called “Nian”. Nian slept all the time from January to December without eating anything. On the Chinese New Year’s Eve, as soon as the sky went dark, Nian went out to search for food. Nian ate animals, such as chickens, ducks, people, and so on. This made everyone very frightened and unable to live a normal life. They had no choice but to take some food and rush to the mountains.

text.traditional: 有一年除夕，一個老太太和她先生不願意離開家。他們家很窮，只有一點米，什麼食物都沒有。而且老太太覺得他們家只有兩口人，年紀都大了，讓怪獸給吃了也無所謂。
text.simplified: 有一年除夕，一个老太太和她先生不愿意离开家。他们家很穷，只有一点米，什么食物都没有。而且老太太觉得他们家只有两口人，年纪都大了，让怪兽给吃了也无所谓。
text.pinyin: Yǒu yì nián chúxī, yíge lǎotàitai hé tā xiānshēng bú yuànyì líkāi jiā. Tāmen jiā hěn qióng, zhǐyǒu yìdiǎn mǐ, shénme shíwù dōu méiyǒu. Érqiě lǎotàitai juéde tāmen jiā zhǐyǒu liǎng kǒu rén, niánjì dōu dà le, ràng guàishòu gěi chī le yě wúsuǒwèi.
text.english: On one Chinese New Year’s Eve, an old lady and her husband didn’t want to leave their home. They were very poor. They had no food except for a little rice. Furthermore, the old lady thought there were only two people in the family, and both were in old age, so they did not care if they were eaten.

text.traditional: 那天下午，老太太的家門口忽然出現了一個老人，他請老太太分一點東西給他吃。老太太覺得他很可憐，就煮了一點兒飯請他吃。老人一邊吃，一邊跟老太太說：「妳不用怕『年』，只要準備幾張紅紙、一些竹子，就可以把『年』趕走了。」
text.simplified: 那天下午，老太太的家门口忽然出现了一个老人，他请老太太分一点东西给他吃。老太太觉得他很可怜，就煮了一点儿饭请他吃。老人一边吃，一边跟老太太说：「你不用怕『年』，只要准备几张红纸、一些竹子，就可以把『年』赶走了。」
text.pinyin: Nà tiān xiàwǔ, lǎotàitai de jiā ménkǒu hūrán chūxiàn le yíge lǎorén, tā qǐng lǎotàitai fēn yìdiǎn dōngxi gěi tā chī. Lǎotàitai juéde tā hěn kělián, jiù zhǔ le yìdiǎnr fàn qǐng tā chī. Lǎorén yìbiān chī, yìbiān gēn lǎotàitai shuō: “Nǐ búyòng pà “nián”, zhǐyào zhǔnbèi jǐ zhāng hóng zhǐ, yìxiē zhúzi, jiù kěyǐ bǎ “nián” gǎn zǒu le.”
text.english: That afternoon, an old man appeared suddenly in front of their house door. He asked the old lady to give him something to eat. The old lady thought he was very pitiful, so she cooked a little rice for him. While the old man was eating, he said: “You don’t need to be afraid of Nian. As long as you prepare a few sheets of red paper and some bamboo, you can drive it away.”

text.traditional: 天剛黑，「年」就真的來了。「年」看見了門上的紅紙、地上燒竹子的火，又聽見燒竹子的時候大大的聲音，就嚇得跑走了。原來，「年」怕的就是：紅色、亮亮的東西和很大的聲音。
text.simplified: 天刚黑，「年」就真的来了。「年」看见了门上的红纸、地上烧竹子的火，又听见烧竹子的时候大大的声音，就吓得跑走了。原来，「年」怕的就是：红色、亮亮的东西和很大的声音。
text.pinyin: Tiān gāng hēi, “nián” jiù zhēnde lái le. “Nián” kànjiàn le mén shàng de hóng zhǐ, dì shàng shāo zhúzi de huǒ, yòu tīngjiàn shāo zhúzi de shíhòu dàdà de shēngyīn, jiù xià de pǎo zǒu le. Yuánlái, “nián” pà de jiùshì: hóngsè, liàng liàng de dōngxi hé hěn dà de shēngyīn.
text.english: When the sky just got dark, Nian did come. As soon as Nian saw the red paper at the door, a fire that burned bamboo on the ground, and heard the loud sound made by the burning bamboo, it became so scared that it ran away. It turned out that Nian was afraid of red, bright things and loud sounds.

text.traditional: 第二天，大家從山上回來時，發現老太太和她先生沒被「年」吃了，都覺得很奇怪。老太太說，要不是老人告訴她把「年」嚇走的方法，他們就被吃了。
text.simplified: 第二天，大家从山上回来时，发现老太太和她先生没被「年」吃了，都觉得很奇怪。老太太说，要不是老人告诉她把「年」吓走的方法，他们就被吃了。
text.pinyin: Dì'èr tiān, dàjiā cóng shān shàng huílái shí, fāxiàn lǎotàitai hé tā xiānshēng méi bèi “nián” chī le, dōu juéde hěn qíguài. Lǎotàitai shuō, yàobúshì lǎorén gàosu tā bǎ “nián” xià zǒu de fāngfǎ, tāmen jiù bèi chī le.
text.english: The next day, everybody came back from the mountains and found it strange that the old lady and her husband were not eaten by Nian. The old lady said that if the old man hadn’t told her how to scare Nian away, they would have been eaten.

text.traditional: 從那個時候起，每年的除夕，大家都會在門口貼紅紙、燒竹子。這就是為什麼中國人在過年的時候，要貼春聯、放鞭炮了。
text.simplified: 从那个时候起，每年的除夕，大家都会在门口贴红纸、烧竹子。这就是为什么中国人在过年的时候，要贴春联、放鞭炮了。
text.pinyin: Cóng nà ge shíhòu qǐ, měi nián de chúxī, dàjiā dōu huì zài ménkǒu tiē hóng zhǐ, shāo zhúzi. Zhè jiù shì wèishénme Zhōngguó rén zài guònián de shíhòu, yào tiē chūnlián, fàng biānpào le.
text.english: From then on, every Chinese New Year’s Eve, everyone pastes red paper on their door and burns bamboo. This is also the very reason why the Chinese paste spring couplets and set off firecrackers during the Chinese New Year.

items.title: Grammar 1–4 · The Thing that Confucius Did Not Know

dialogue.title: 對話 · 孔子不知道的事 · The Thing that Confucius Did Not Know

text.traditional: （學校附近的飲料店）
text.simplified: （学校附近的饮料店）
text.pinyin: (Xuéxiào fùjìn de yǐnliào diàn)
text.english: (At a drink shop near the school.)

text.traditional: 良介，你知道我們學校九月二十八號為什麼放假嗎？
text.simplified: 良介，你知道我们学校九月二十八号为什么放假吗？
text.pinyin: Liángjiè, nǐ zhīdào wǒmen xuéxiào jiǔ yuè èrshíbā hào wèishénme fàngjià ma?
text.english: Ryosuke, do you know why we have a school holiday on September 28th?

text.traditional: 我不知道。為什麼呢？
text.simplified: 我不知道。为什么呢？
text.pinyin: Wǒ bù zhīdào. Wèishénme ne?
text.english: No, I don't know. Why?

text.traditional: 因為那天是孔子的生日，也是台灣的「教師節」。
text.simplified: 因为那天是孔子的生日，也是台湾的「教师节」。
text.pinyin: Yīnwèi nà tiān shì Kǒngzǐ de shēngrì, yě shì Táiwān de “Jiàoshījié”.
text.english: It is because that day is Confucius' birthday. It's also the Teachers' Day in Taiwan.

text.traditional: 我聽過孔子，可是知道的不多。
text.simplified: 我听过孔子，可是知道的不多。
text.pinyin: Wǒ tīng guo Kǒngzǐ, kěshì zhīdào de bù duō.
text.english: I've heard about Confucius, but I don't know much about him.

text.traditional: 那我就給你們說一個孔子的故事吧。
text.simplified: 那我就给你们说一个孔子的故事吧。
text.pinyin: Nà wǒ jiù gěi nǐmen shuō yíge Kǒngzǐ de gùshì ba.
text.english: Then, I'll tell you a story about Confucius!

text.traditional: 太棒了！我雖然是日本人，但是對中國文化可有興趣了。快點兒說！
text.simplified: 太棒了！我虽然是日本人，但是对中国文化可有兴趣了。快点儿说！
text.pinyin: Tài bàng le! Wǒ suīrán shì Rìběn rén, dànshì duì Zhōngguó wénhuà kě yǒu xìngqù le. Kuài diǎnr shuō!
text.english: Great! Although I'm Japanese, I'm quite interested in Chinese culture. Tell me quickly!

text.traditional: 有一天，孔子和學生子路到了一個美麗的地方，遇到了兩個小孩……
text.simplified: 有一天，孔子和学生子路到了一个美丽的地方，遇到了两个小孩……
text.pinyin: Yǒu yì tiān, Kǒngzǐ hé xuéshēng Zǐlù dào le yíge měilì de dìfāng, yùdào le liǎng ge xiǎohái…
text.english: One day, Confucius and his student Zilu went to a very beautiful place and met two children...

text.traditional: 子路，把船停在那座橋旁邊，我們休息一下。
text.simplified: 子路，把船停在那座桥旁边，我们休息一下。
text.pinyin: Zǐlù, bǎ chuán tíng zài nà zuò qiáo pángbiān, wǒmen xiūxí yíxià.
